The presentation, ranks, and exceptional types — Let $X$ be a connected closed oriented topological surface of genus $g$, let $S$ consist of $
u$ distinct points, and put $U=X\setminus S$. A discrete group with loops of type $(g,
u)$ consists of a group $\pi$, a finite index set $I$ of cardinality $
u$, a free rank-one integral orientation module $T$, and exterior homomorphisms $\kappa_i:T	o\pi$. Here an exterior homomorphism is a conjugacy class, under conjugation in the target, of actual homomorphisms. After choosing a generator of $T$, representatives $c_i=\kappa_i(1)$, an ordering of $I$, and the handle generators, these data admit the presentation \[ \pi_{g,

When $I$ is empty one additionally identifies $T$ with the dual of $H^2(\pi;\Z)$, or its continuous profinite counterpart. This is the covariant orientation convention of scan 116. More precisely, an earlier cohomological marking $\kappa:H^2(\pi;\Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{\mathrm{coh}}$ on scan 91 gives, by dualization, $\kappa^\vee:T_{\mathrm{coh}}^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}H_2(\pi;\Z)$; the covariant module used here is $T=T_{\mathrm{coh}}^\vee$. The same typed dual map specifies the profinite convention. For an isomorphism of groups with loops the data are an isomorphism $f:\pi	o\pi_1$, a bijection $s:I	o I_1$, and an isomorphism $t:T	o T_1$ such that $f\kappa_i$ is conjugate to $\kappa_{s(i)}t$ for every $i$, with the corresponding dual-cohomology compatibility when $I$ is empty. An exterior group with loops regards two such $f$ as equivalent when they differ by target inner conjugation, with the same $s,t$. Thus its isomorphism sets are explicitly the quotient of the preceding isomorphism sets by $\Inn(\pi_1)$. In all nontrivial admitted types $L_i=\kappa_i(T)$ recovers its source by A.2; the one-puncture sphere requires the original source map. For $

The same list holds for their profinite completions. The peripheral maps from the source orientation group $\Z$ to $\pi$ are injective except at $(0,1)$, among the types admitted in scans 91--92. statement: Discrete peripheral rigidity in every hyperbolic type — For $2g+\nu>2$, the group $\pi=\pi_{g,\nu}$ has trivial centre and $C_\pi(H)=1$ for every finite-index subgroup $H$. For every peripheral subgroup and every integer $n\ge1$, \[ N_\pi(L_i)=C_\pi(L_i)=C_\pi(L_i^n)=L_i. \] Distinct peripheral indices give distinct, noncommensurable conjugacy classes.

statement: Exact exceptional-case table — The discrete and profinite exceptional groups have the following properties; in the profinite column replace $\Z$ by $\widehat\Z$. \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} (g,\nu)&\pi& Z(\pi)&C_\pi(H)\ (H\text{ finite index/open})&\text{peripherals}\\\hline (0,0)&1&1&1&\text{none}\\ (0,1)&1&1&1&L_1=1\\ (0,2)&\Z&\Z&\Z&L_1=L_2=\pi\\ (1,0)&\Z^2&\Z^2&\Z^2&\text{none} \end{array} \] Consequently the peripheral normalizer and power-centralizer equalities hold in the plane and annulus, while distinctness of the two peripheral classes fails on the annulus. The nonzero vector $1$ on the annulus and $(1,0)$ on the torus witness failure of both centre and finite-index-centralizer assertions. The plane's failure is the noninjective source map, not a nontrivial centre. For the standard base-element formula of scan 501, the annulus satisfies the equality since its basis element generates its whole group. On the torus $C(\langle(1,0)\rangle^n)=\Z^2$ for every $n\ge1$, and $(0,1)$ witnesses its failure to equal $\langle(1,0)\rangle$. The same vector works after completion. The sphere and plane have no nontrivial base elements to test.

statement: Peripheral decomposition groups and transporters — Let $1\to\pi\to E\xrightarrow{p}\Gamma\to1$ arise from an action on a hyperbolic marked surface. Choose one peripheral subgroup $L_s$ and the corresponding peripheral lift group $E_s\subset E$; thus $E_s\cap\pi=L_s$ and $p(E_s)=\Gamma_s$, the stabilizer of that puncture. Define \[ \operatorname{Trans}_E(L_s^d,L_s) =\{e\in E:eL_s^de^{-1}\subseteq L_s\}\qquad(d\ge1). \] Then $N_E(L_s)=\operatorname{Trans}_E(L_s^d,L_s)=E_s$. The same assertions hold for the corresponding profinite extension and closed peripheral groups. On the annulus these assertions fail for $z\mapsto1/z$: with $E=\Z\rtimes C_2$ and the involution acting by inversion, $E_s=\Z$ but $N_E(L_s)=E$ and every transporter is $E$. More generally for every annulus action both normalizer and transporter equal $E$, while $E_s$ is the inverse image of the end stabilizer. Thus their equality with $E_s$ holds exactly when the action fixes both ends. On the one-puncture sphere the peripheral mixed group maps onto $E=\Gamma$ with kernel $\Z$; using its image, both equalities hold, whereas identifying that mixed group itself with a subgroup is invalid. The closed sphere and torus have no peripheral statement.

statement: Centre-free extension reconstruction and its abelian correction — For a centre-free discrete group $\pi$ and a homomorphism $\rho:\Gamma\to\Out(\pi)$, the extension inducing $\rho$ is, up to a unique isomorphism inducing the identity on its prescribed kernel and quotient, \[ E_\rho=\{(a,\gamma)\in\Aut(\pi)\times\Gamma:[a]=\rho(\gamma)\}. \] The same formula holds for a topologically finitely generated centre-free profinite $\pi$ and continuous $\rho$, with the profinite topology. For $A=\Z$ or $\Z^2$ and a prescribed action $\rho:\Gamma\to\Aut(A)$, extension classes with their kernel and quotient identified are instead classified by $H^2(\Gamma;A_\rho)$. Their automorphisms inducing the identity on both ends form $Z^1(\Gamma;A_\rho)$. For finite $\Gamma$ this statement holds with $A=\widehat\Z$ or $\widehat\Z^2$ and continuous cochains. Thus both the annulus and the torus require the abelian correction.

statement: The full profinite rigidity statements, with reductions — For the full profinite completion $\Pi=\widehat\pi_{g,\nu}$ of a hyperbolic type, $\Pi$ is torsion-free, $C_\Pi(H)=1$ for every open subgroup $H$, and \[ N_\Pi(\widehat L_i)=C_\Pi(\widehat L_i^n)=\widehat L_i \quad(n\in\Z_{>0}). \] Distinct peripheral classes are noncommensurable. The same conclusions hold for the pro-$p$ completions, for every prime $p$, including $2$ and $3$. The four exceptional types have exactly the completed table of A.4, and A.5 supplies the extension and transporter assertions.

statement: Lemme 5 from open-subgroup centralizers alone — Let $P$ be a discrete or profinite group for which the centralizer of every finite-index, respectively open, subgroup is trivial. Let $H\subset P$ be such a subgroup and let $u\in\Aut(P)$ preserve $H$. An automorphism restricting to the identity on $H$ is the identity on $P$. An automorphism whose restriction equals $\operatorname{conj}_h$ for some $h\in H$ equals $\operatorname{conj}_h$ on $P$.

statement: Faithfulness ascends along a finite etale cover — Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, $U/k$ a hyperbolic geometrically connected smooth curve, and $V\to U$ a finite etale geometrically connected covering defined over $k$. Put $\Gamma=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline k/k)$ and choose compatible geometric base points. Faithfulness of $\Gamma\to\Out(\pi_1(U_{\overline k}))$ implies faithfulness of $\Gamma\to\Out(\pi_1(V_{\overline k}))$.

Then $\Lambda\simeq\widehat\Z$ and, for every positive integer $n$, \[ C_\Pi(\Lambda^n)=N_\Pi(\Lambda^n)=\Lambda. \]

statement: What the abstract profinite presentation specifies — The full profinite presentation required by scan 318, equation (4), already determines a profinite group with loops isomorphic to $\widehat\pi_{g,\nu}$ with its standard loops. Hence A.7 and A.10 apply to every abstract object satisfying that presentation axiom. Merely requiring generators to satisfy the displayed equation would not suffice: $P=\widehat\Z^2$, $c_1=(1,0)$, $c_2=(0,1)$, $c_3=(-1,-1)$ satisfies the $(0,3)$ relation, has three injective procyclic peripheral subgroups and the rank-one orientation kernel, but has centre $P$.

statement:
The discrete filling isomorphism and all compatibility maps — Let $U=X\setminus S$ be hyperbolic, choose $b\in U$, and put $U'=U\setminus\{b\}$, $\pi'=\pi_1(U')$, and $\pi=\pi'/\langle\!\langle L_bangle\!angle$. Choose the peripheral representative $L_b\subset\pi'$. The normalization of representatives defines an isomorphism of discrete groups \[ d_b:\Out_{\mathrm{lac}}(\pi';b)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Aut_{\mathrm{lac}}(\pi). \] On both sides old punctures may be permuted and orientation may be reversed. It identifies the pure orientation-preserving subgroups, whose common index is $2
u!$, where $
u=|S|$. It commutes with forgetting the distinguished puncture, with the maps to $\Out_{\mathrm{lac}}(\pi)$, with orientation characters, with the permutation maps to $\mathfrak S_
u$, and with point-pushing and inner conjugation on their kernels.

statement: Filling into the two abelian targets — Exactly one of the drilled and filled groups is abelian in the two cases $(0,3)\to(0,2)$ and $(1,1)\to(1,0)$. In the first, the homomorphism on automorphisms of the underlying groups with peripheral subgroup classes is \[ C_2\times C_2=\Out_{\mathrm{lac}}(F_2;[\langle xy\rangle]) \longrightarrow\Aut(\Z)=C_2, \] with kernel of order two. Its nontrivial element has representative $x\mapsto y^{-1}$, $y\mapsto x^{-1}$. Its restriction to the positive-orientation subgroup is an isomorphism. Retaining the two indexed peripheral source maps and their orientation line on the annulus enlarges the target automorphism group to $C_2\times C_2$ and restores the full isomorphism. In the second case the filling map is the isomorphism $\operatorname{GL}_2(\Z)\to\operatorname{GL}_2(\Z)$, with positive subgroup $\operatorname{SL}_2(\Z)$.

statement: Primitive loops in finite-step solvable quotients — Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty set of primes, $F$ a free pro-$\Sigma$ group of finite rank at least two, and $F^{[j]}$ its closed derived series. Put $F_m=F/F^{[m]}$, $m\ge2$. For any element $x$ of a free basis and any positive integer $n$, \[ C_{F_m}(x^n)=N_{F_m}(\overline{\langle x\rangle}) =\overline{\langle x\rangle}\simeq\Z_\Sigma, \qquad \Z_\Sigma=\prod_{p\in\Sigma}\Z_p. \] Every open subgroup of $F_m$ has trivial centralizer. For $\nu\ge2$, all peripheral loops of the pro-$\Sigma$ group of type $(g,\nu)$ satisfy these formulas in every $F_m$. Their indexed conjugacy classes are pairwise distinct in all hyperbolic types.

statement: The compact intersection calculation used in descent — Let $(H_\alpha)$ be a decreasing directed family of closed subgroups of a profinite group $P$, and put $K=\bigcap_\alpha H_\alpha$. Then \[ K^{[j]}=\bigcap_\alpha H_\alpha^{[j]}\quad(j\ge0). \] For a closed subgroup $L\subset P$ and decreasing closed normal subgroups $N_\alpha$ of $P$, one also has $\bigcap_\alpha LN_\alpha=L(\bigcap_\alpha N_\alpha)$.

statement: The one-puncture solvable threshold, with a finite certificate — Let $F$ be the pro-$\Sigma$ completion of $\pi_{g,1}$, $g\ge1$, let $c=\prod_{j=1}^g[a_j,b_j]$ (the inverse peripheral generator), and write $c$ for its image in $F_m=F/F^{[m]}$. For every positive integer $n$, \[ \begin{array}{ll} m=2:& C_{F_2}(c^n)=N_{F_2}(\overline{\langle c\rangle})=F_2',\\[2pt] m\ge3:&C_{F_m}(c^n)=N_{F_m}(\overline{\langle c\rangle}) =\overline{\langle c\rangle}. \end{array} \] In the first line the inclusion $\overline{\langle c\rangle}\subset F_2'$ is strict. Thus peripheral rigidity fails at the smallest solvable depth $m=2$ and is restored at every $m\ge3$, for the full profinite and every pro-$p$ version.

For every $m\ge2$, $P_m$ is torsion-free and centre-free. This verifies the form of \cite[Theorem 2.9 and Corollary 2.10]{A_Yamaguchi2026} needed here by the following argument from finite covers and transfer.

statement:
The remaining affine solvable rigidity list and a closed bound — For all hyperbolic types with $
u>0$, and all $m\ge2$, the maximal $m$-step-solvable full profinite or pro-$\Sigma$ quotient has trivial centre and trivial centralizers of open subgroups, and is torsion-free. Peripheral conjugacy classes remain distinct. For $
u\ge2$ all peripheral normalizer and integer-power-centralizer equalities hold at every $m\ge2$; for $
u=1$ their exact values are those of A.16. In an extension obtained by quotienting a geometric action extension by the $m$th closed derived subgroup of its kernel, the equality $N_E(L_s)=E_s$ holds in the former cases and at $m\ge3$ in the latter. At $
u=1,m=2$ its correct value is $N_E(L_s)=F_2'E_s$, with the intersection $F_2'\cap E_s=L_s$. In all these cases every transporter $\operatorname{Trans}_E(L_s^d,L_s)$, $d\ge1$, equals the same displayed normalizer. Since the kernels are centre-free by A.17, the extension reconstruction of A.6 also applies to all these solvable quotients. Standard free-basis generators satisfy the power-centralizer formula at every $m\ge2$ by A.14. For a closed hyperbolic group $P$ and an open subgroup $H\subset P_m$, the proven universal bound is \[ C_{P_m}(H)\subseteq P_m^{[m-1]}. \]

statement: Closed finite-step power centralizers and slimness — Let $P$ be the pro-$\Sigma$ completion of a closed oriented surface group of genus $g\ge2$, let $m\ge2$, and put $P_m=P/P^{[m]}$. Let $x$ be represented by a nonseparating simple closed curve, in particular by any standard handle generator. Then for every positive integer $n$, \[ C_{P_m}(x^n)=N_{P_m}(\overline{\langle x^n\rangle}) =\overline{\langle x\rangle}\simeq\Z_\Sigma. \] Consequently $C_{P_m}(H)=1$ for every open subgroup $H$. This includes the full profinite and every pro-$p$ quotient, without a restriction at $p=2$ or $3$.

statement: The typed completion comparison for filling — For the two hyperbolic groups in A.12, put $\Pi'=\widehat{\pi'}$ and $\Pi=\widehat\pi$. There is a commutative diagram of profinite groups \[ \begin{array}{ccc} \widehat{\Out_{\mathrm{lac}}(\pi';b)} &\xrightarrow{\ \widehat{d_b}\ }& \widehat{\Aut_{\mathrm{lac}}(\pi)}\\ \big\downarrow c_{\mathrm{out}}&&\big\downarrow c_{\mathrm{aut}}\\ \Out_{\mathrm{lac}}(\Pi';b) &\xrightarrow{\ d_b^{\mathrm{cont}}\ }& \Aut_{\mathrm{lac}}(\Pi). \end{array} \] The upper horizontal map is an isomorphism. The lower horizontal map is the normalized filling homomorphism on all continuous loop automorphisms. The vertical maps are induced by extending discrete automorphisms to group completions. The same construction with pro-$p$ completions of the surface groups still has the full profinite completions of the discrete automorphism groups in its upper row. These assertions specify the precise consequence of the discrete filling theorem; no isomorphism assertion for the lower horizontal or vertical arrows is used.

statement: Finite plane actions and simultaneous local models — Every faithful action of a finite group $H$ on $\R^2$ by homeomorphisms is conjugate to an orthogonal action. When $H^+\ne1$, $H^+$ is cyclic, $H$ is cyclic or dihedral, and $(\R^2)^H$ is a single point. A nontrivial orientation-reversing involution has a fixed line. Every stabilizer in a finite action on a surface with universal cover $\R^2$ has an invariant disc on which the whole stabilizer acts by an orthogonal action. These conclusions supply the two local assertions used in \S15, folios 70--74, scans 141--149, and \S33, scan 440.

statement: The omitted orientation hypothesis in scans 146--147 — The displayed lemma on scan 147, taken without its preceding orientation hypothesis, is false. Its correct form is: an orientation-preserving finite-order homeomorphism $u$ of $\C$ commuting with $T(z)=z+1$ and satisfying $u(0)=0$ is the identity. The quotient $\C/\Z$ provides a complete proof along the route proposed in the manuscript.

statement: Sections and isolated fixed points — Let $\widetilde U\cong\R^2$. A faithful finite action on $U$ with $G^+\ne1$ has a bijection \[ U^G\longrightarrow \operatorname{Sec}(E\to G)/\pi. \] For every section subgroup $K$, $C_\pi(K)=1$. Existence of a section forces $G$ to be cyclic or dihedral. More generally, every nontrivial finite subgroup of $E$ whose orientation-preserving part is nontrivial is contained in exactly one maximal finite subgroup of $E$. For an orientation-preserving action the map from points with nontrivial stabilizer to maximal partial-section classes is a $G$-equivariant bijection. These are the theorem and corollary of \S15, folios 73--75, scans 148--151, with their stated orientation hypotheses.

statement: Reflection sections, ovals, and punctured ovals — Let $\sigma$ be an orientation-reversing involution of $U$ with $\widetilde U\cong\R^2$, and let $E\to C_2$ be its lift extension. There is a bijection \[ \pi_0(U^\sigma)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sec}(E\to C_2)/\pi. \] For the section $s$ associated with a component $Z$, inclusion induces an isomorphism $\pi_1(Z)\cong C_\pi(s)$. Thus the centralizer is $1$ for a line and $\Z$ for an oval. This includes punctures fixed or permuted by $\sigma$ and proves \S33, folios 222--225, scans 440--445, in the required noncompact cases.

statement: Recovering the incidence and cyclic order of real punctures — For a hyperbolic $U=X\setminus S$ with anti-involution $\sigma$, its discrete extension together with its indexed peripheral subgroups determines the following finite graph. Its vertices are the section classes of B.4, its edges are the real punctures, and each edge is attached to its two adjacent real half-branches. Every punctured oval gives one cycle, allowing a loop or two parallel edges. The graph recovers which punctures lie on each oval and their cyclic order up to reversal. Unpunctured ovals are the vertices with infinite cyclic centralizer. The claim uses the extension and peripheral incidence maps; a naked set of section classes alone has no such incidence information.

statement: The fundamental loop lemma of \S18 — Let $\pi=\pi_1(U)$ be hyperbolic and discrete, with its indexed peripheral structure and orientation module. A finite-order orientation-preserving automorphism of $\pi$ fixing a peripheral index and normalizing its subgroup $L_i$ is the identity. Consequently the peripheral extension attached to a nontrivial finite-order positive outer automorphism fixing $i$ cannot split. statement: An intrinsic discrete formula for the multiplier — For a geometric finite extension of a hyperbolic discrete surface group, $E$ with its peripheral structure and orientation module $T$ determines $\mu_E$ on all torsion elements. On $E^+$ it is the rotation number of its canonical oriented boundary action. More explicitly, let $\widetilde{\operatorname{Homeo}}^+(S^1)\to\operatorname{Homeo}^+(S^1)$ be the central extension by the positively oriented deck translation $z$. For $u\in E^+$ of order $n$ and any lift $\widetilde u$, write $\widetilde u^{,n}=z^k$. Then \[ \mu_E(u)=\frac{k}{n}\pmod{\Z}\quad\hbox{in }T\otimes\Q/\Z. \] For a nonidentity orientation-reversing torsion element we put $\mu_E(u)$ equal to the unique nonzero element of order two. With this convention the formula is natural under isomorphisms preserving the loops and transporting $T$, satisfies $\mu(u^m)=m\mu(u)$, and has the same order as $u$. This answers the discrete intrinsicity question of \S15, folios 77--79, scans 155--160.

statement: Finite annulus and torus actions, and their multipliers — Every finite topological action on the torus is topologically conjugate to an affine action on $V/\Lambda$, where $\Lambda\cong\Z^2$ and $V=\Lambda\otimes\R$. For a fixed finite operator group $G$ such an action is specified by a homomorphism $A:G\to GL(\Lambda)$ and a cocycle $b\in Z^1(G,V/\Lambda)$, subject to faithfulness of $g\mapsto(x\mapsto A_gx+b_g)$. Translation conjugacy corresponds exactly to a coboundary, and \[ H^1(G,V/\Lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2(G,\Lambda) \] is the connecting homomorphism. Linear changes of the lattice give the further conjugacies. Every finite annulus action has a simultaneous normal form \[ (x,t)\longmapsto(\epsilon_g x+a_g,\eta_g t), \qquad x\in\R/\Z,\quad t\in\R,\quad \epsilon_g,\eta_g\in\{1,-1\}. \] These descriptions determine the multiplier of every finite-order element in the respective lift extensions.

statement: Complete topological classification of anti-involutions — Conjugacy classes of anti-involutions of a closed oriented genus-$g$ surface are classified by the orientability of the quotient and its number $b$ of boundary components. statement: The two centralizer corollaries in both quotient families — Let $g\ge2$, and let an anti-involution of $X_g$ have $b>0$ ovals, with outer class $\sigma$. There are exactly $b$ classes of order-two genuine loop automorphisms lifting $\sigma$, under conjugacy by $\pi_g$. For each lift $u$, $\pi_g^u\cong\Z$. The positive centralizer of $\sigma$ acts transitively on those $b$ classes. More precisely, writing $A=\Aut_{\rm lac}(\pi_g)$ and $O=\Out_{\rm lac}(\pi_g)$, there is an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow\pi_g^u\longrightarrow C_{A^+}(u) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Stab}_{C_{O^+}(\sigma)}([u])\longrightarrow1, \] and the last group has index $b$ in $C_{O^+}(\sigma)$. statement: The tube twists, their maximality property, and their normalizer — For $g\ge2$, the elements $\rho_j$ of \S33, scans 453--470, are full Dehn twists about a cut system $c_1,\ldots,c_g$: disjoint nonseparating curves with connected complement. They generate $H\cong\Z^g$. This is not a maximal free abelian subgroup of $\mathcal T_g$: it is contained in a multitwist subgroup of rank $3g-3$. It has the precise maximality property of being a full multitwist group of largest rank whose supporting multicurve has connected complement. Furthermore \[ N_{\mathcal T_g}(H)=\operatorname{Stab}_{\mathcal T_g}(\{c_1,\ldots,c_g\}), \qquad N_{\mathcal T_g}(H)/C_{\mathcal T_g}(H)\cong S_g\times C_2. \] The action on $H$ permutes its basis and multiplies every basis vector by the same orientation sign. Cutting and capping gives an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow H\longrightarrow N_{\mathcal T_g}(H) \longrightarrow\mathcal T^{\rm pairs}_{0,2g}\longrightarrow1, \] where the last extended sphere mapping class group preserves the partition of its $2g$ punctures into the $g$ unordered gluing pairs.

statement: Relations for arbitrary strips and a uniform obstruction to generation — Choose for each $c_j$ one simple transversal $d_j$, using a strip in the complement of the other tubes, so that $i(c_i,d_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Its supported subgroup is the central extension $\langle A_j,B_j\rangle\cong B_3$ of B.21, with quotient $SL_2(\Z)$. statement: The oriented drilling equivalence and the bijection — Fix a finite group $\Gamma$ and faithful orientation-preserving outer actions on discrete hyperbolic groups with loops. statement: Principal-kernel boundary comparison and controlled planar fillings — Let $f_t,G$ be the original plane loop and its generated group, and let $O$ be an open $G$-orbit with one-dimensional full local centralizer. Retain the actual principal quotient of C.33, \[ \pi_0:O\longrightarrow B_0=O/C_O^0, \qquad \beta:G\longrightarrow\operatorname{Homeo}(B_0). \tag{C.65.1} \] Let $N$ consist of endpoints $h_1$ of paths \[ \begin{gathered} h_s=\prod_{j=1}^{m}f_{a_j(s)}^{\epsilon_j}, \qquad a_j:[0,1]\to[0,1]\ \text{continuous},\\ \epsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}, \qquad h_0=\id,\qquad\beta(h_s)=\id\ \text{for every }s. \end{gathered} \tag{C.65.2} \] The finite length and signs may depend on the path. For every nontrivial nonopen $G$-orbit $B\subset\partial O$ whose actual intrinsic restriction image $\rho_B(G)$ is nonmetabelian, \[ \rho_B(N)=1,\qquad \rho_B:G\longrightarrow\operatorname{Homeo}(B). \tag{C.65.3} \] In particular two actual finite-word paths $p_s,q_s$ starting at the identity and satisfying $\beta(p_s)=\beta(q_s)$ for every $s$ have exactly the same restriction to each such $B$ at every time. For the full principal kernel $K_0=\ker\beta$, the image $D_B=\rho_B(K_0)$ is central in $\rho_B(G)$ and is a closed discrete cyclic subgroup of the intrinsic homeomorphism group of $B$; it is finite when $B$ is a circle. Give \[ E_B=\{(\beta(g),\rho_B(g)):g\in G\} \subset\operatorname{Homeo}(B_0) \times\operatorname{Homeo}(B) \] the actual induced product topology, and put $\Delta_B=\{1\}\times D_B$. There are exact maps \[ E_B\longrightarrow E_B/\Delta_B \longrightarrow\beta(G). \] The first map is a covering with deck group $\Delta_B$; the second is a continuous bijective homomorphism onto the actual induced image $\beta(G)$. No continuity of its inverse is asserted. There is also the following controlled filling fact for the same planar setting. For any open planar set $V$, any open Euclidean disk $D$, and any connected component $U$ of $V\cap D$, the actual inclusion induces an injection \[ \pi_1(U,x)\longrightarrow\pi_1(V,x) \qquad(x\in U). \tag{C.65.4} \] Thus a based loop in $U$ null-homotopic in $V$ has a based disk filling entirely in $U$. statement: Zero-dimensional frontiers give a global centralizer filling — Let $f_t$ be a based ambient-null loop in $\operatorname{Homeo}^+(\R^2)$, let $G$ be the group generated by its values, and let $H$ be any group of plane homeomorphisms commuting with every $f_t$. statement: The exact relative disk group for a locally connected frontier — Let $O\subset\R^2$ be a nonempty bounded simply connected open set with locally connected frontier. In particular $\mathcal K_O$ is contractible. The frontier need not be a Jordan curve. For the actual stabilizer $H_O$ of $O$ in any specified group of ambient operators, let \[ \eta_q:H_O\longrightarrow \operatorname{Homeo}(\overline{\mathbb D}) \tag{C.67.4} \] be its original prime-end action in the chosen Riemann coordinate. statement: Operator-compatible carriers for the original evaluation fillings — Let $f_t$, $G$, $H$ and the $H$-invariant union $W$ of original open $G$-orbits be as in C.64. statement: Actual disk comparisons for two-dimensional operators and a cyclic compactification — Let $Q$ be a closed locally compact subgroup of $\operatorname{Homeo}(\mathbb D)$, with its actual compact-open and inverse topology, acting freely and properly on $\mathbb D$. In particular every based loop fills there. No extension of the $Q$-action to the boundary, and no closed-disk conjugacy for that action, is assumed. If $A\leq\operatorname{Homeo}(\overline{\mathbb D})$ has actual restricted closure $Q$, then $E_Q=C_{\mathcal D_\partial}(A)$ by continuity on the interior and density in the closed disk. There is also an explicit cyclic action on the actual closed disk whose interior image is closed, discrete, free and proper, and which admits no closed-disk conjugacy to a torsion-free cyclic Fuchsian action. For its specified invariant partial compactification, the analogue of the restriction isomorphism (C.69.2) is not surjective. The proof gives the actual maps witnessing both assertions. Nevertheless its boundary-fixed centralizer is contractible: it is identified topologically with an explicitly described group of continuous families of increasing real lifts, and linear interpolation supplies the contraction. Its interior orbits are precisely the displayed vertical lines, so this example does not supply an open transitive orbit for that boundary-fixed centralizer.

statement: The exact prime-end comparison for arbitrary simply connected frontiers — Let $O\subset S^2$ be a simply connected domain with nondegenerate frontier, and fix a conformal map $\phi:\mathbb D\to O$. Retain the actual groups \[ K_O=\{h\in\operatorname{Homeo}^+(S^2): h|_{S^2\setminus O}=\id\}, \qquad \mathcal D_\partial =\operatorname{Homeo}(\overline{\mathbb D},S^1). \tag{C.73.1} \] Every $h\in K_O$ induces the identity on the prime-end circle of $O$. Its actual prime-end extension defines a continuous injective homomorphism \[ \begin{split} \iota_O:K_O&\longrightarrow\mathcal D_\partial,\\ \iota_O(h)|_{\mathbb D}&=\phi^{-1}h\phi . \end{split} \tag{C.73.2} \] All groups have the compact-open and inverse topologies. The image of (C.73.2) is dense. For locally connected frontier it is the topological isomorphism of C.68. For every non-locally-connected frontier its image is proper, and its inverse on that image is not continuous. The proof supplies the actual sequences and a disk map witnessing these two failures. Every actual ambient operator preserving $O$ induces its own prime-end map, and (C.73.2) intertwines conjugation by the original operator with conjugation by that prime-end map. In particular it identifies an ambient relative centralizer with the intersection of its image and the corresponding disk centralizer, with the original operator labels and restriction kernel retained. statement: An exact obstruction to principal-coordinate interpolation — There is an explicit based loop $f_\tau\in\mathcal D_\partial$ whose generated group $G$ is transitive on $\mathbb D$ and whose full interior centralizer is a closed free proper group $Q\cong\mathbb R$. statement: The actual orbit strips for a one-dimensional proper operator action — Let $O$ be a plane, including an actual open disk, and let $Q\leq\operatorname{Homeo}(O)$ be closed, locally compact, free and proper, with $\dim Q=1$. Let $f_\tau$ be a continuous based loop in its centralizer, and put $G=\langle f_\tau\rangle$. Retain the actual principal coordinate of C.33, with its inverse, in which \[ \begin{split} O&\cong\mathbb R_s\times\mathbb R_t,\\ f_\tau(s,t)&=(s+u_\tau(t),\beta_\tau(t)),\\ A&=\{t:\beta_\tau(t)=t\text{ for every }\tau\}. \end{split} \tag{C.75.1} \] The set $A$ is closed. On every component $I$ of $\mathbb R\setminus A$, precisely one of the following two descriptions holds. Either $\mathbb R\times I$ is one open $G$-orbit, or there is a continuous function $b_I:I\to\mathbb R$ such that all the orbits in that strip are exactly \[ \{(c+b_I(t),t):t\in I\}, \qquad c\in\mathbb R. \tag{C.75.2} \] In the latter case the actual coordinate $(s,t)\mapsto(s-b_I(t),t)$, with inverse $(w,t)\mapsto(w+b_I(t),t)$, changes every restricted generator to $(w,t)\mapsto(w,\beta_\tau(t))$. The effective restricted action and its base image are topologically isomorphic in their actual compact-open and inverse topologies. At each $a\in A$ the orbits on $\mathbb R\times\{a\}$ are individual points when every $u_\tau(a)$ vanishes, and otherwise that entire horizontal line is one orbit. This lists all orbits. In particular every finite interior frontier line of an open orbit is the actual proper line at an endpoint of its base interval. There are no circular orbits. The graph in (C.75.2) is proper in its indicated strip; extension of $b_I$ to an endpoint is not asserted. There is a further exact comparison for a finite endpoint $a\in A$ of a base interval $I$. Write $g(s,t)=(s+u_g(t),\beta_g(t))$ for the original element $g\in G$, and put \[ c_a(g)=u_g(a),\qquad G_t=\{g\in G:\beta_g(t)=t\}\quad(t\in I). \tag{C.75.3} \] The character $c_a$ is continuous. There are exactly three alternatives: $c_a=0$; or $c_a\ne0$ and $c_a(G_t)=0$; or $c_a(G_t)=\mathbb R$. In the second alternative there is an actual homeomorphism $b:I\to\mathbb R$ satisfying \[ b(\beta_g(t))=b(t)+c_a(g) \qquad(g\in G,\ t\in I). \tag{C.75.4} \] In the third alternative every real endpoint displacement is realized by an actual source element fixing the chosen base point $t$. All component-operator equations and the kernel of the comparison action used below are retained. No continuous choice of these correcting source elements, or frontier filling, is inferred.

statement: Simultaneous endpoint prescriptions with compact original-boundary control — Let $Q$ be the actual closed, locally compact, free proper one-dimensional group on $O=\operatorname{int}\overline D$ of C.75. Let $f_\tau$ be a based loop of homeomorphisms of the actual closed disk, fixing its boundary pointwise and commuting with $Q$ on $O$. Use the actual principal coordinate and its inverse from C.75, with coordinates $(s,t)$, common base fixed set $A$, and generated group $G$. Retain the following components $I$ of $\mathbb R\setminus A$: those for which every finite-endpoint character $c_a$ is zero, and those having a finite endpoint $a$ with \[ c_a\ne0,\qquad c_a(G_t)=0\quad(t\in I). \tag{C.76.1} \] The first prescription includes an interval without finite endpoints. Let $Z\subset\overline D$ consist of the original boundary circle, the actual lines over $A$, and all retained strips. This is a closed subset, preserved by the loop and by every actual interior operator wherever that operator is defined. The restricted loop has a based contraction through homeomorphisms of $Z$, with jointly continuous inverses, fixing the original circle and commuting with every $q\in Q$ on $Z\cap O$. On every line over $a\in A$, the contraction is exactly \[ (s,a)\longmapsto(s+r u_\tau(a),a), \qquad 0\leq r\leq1. \tag{C.76.2} \] On a strip retained by (C.76.1), choose C.75's actual homeomorphism $b:I\to\mathbb R$ for one such endpoint. The base contraction is \[ B_{r,\tau}(t)=b^{-1}\bigl(b(t)+r c_a(f_\tau)\bigr). \tag{C.76.3} \] Both finite endpoint values, when there are two, are prescribed simultaneously by (C.76.2). All original component operators, including negative fiber multipliers, are retained. One compact family of original closed-disk homeomorphisms controls the forward and inverse evaluations over all retained strips and all parameters. Hence the construction includes infinitely many strips accumulating at an interior line or at the original circle. More precisely, let $\mathscr R_Z$ be the subgroup of the original relative $Q$-centralizer preserving $Z$, and let \[ \begin{split} \mathscr A_Z={}&\{k\in\operatorname{Homeo}(Z): k|_{\partial\overline D}=\id, \ kq=qk\text{ on }Z\cap O\},\\ \rho_Z:\mathscr R_Z&\longrightarrow\mathscr A_Z, \qquad \rho_Z(h)=h|_Z. \end{split} \tag{C.76.4} \] These are the actual compact-open and inverse topologies, and $\rho_Z$ is a continuous homomorphism. The contraction just asserted fills the actual loop $\rho_Z(f_\tau)$ in $\mathscr A_Z$. When every complementary interval is retained, $Z=\overline D$ and this is a contraction in the original relative centralizer itself. No lifting of the constructed filling through $\rho_Z$ is asserted for a proper $Z$.

statement: All abelian base strips and the exact remaining character action — Keep the actual closed disk, proper one-dimensional operator group $Q$, loop, principal coordinate, and common base fixed set $A$ of C.76. For a component $I$ of $\mathbb R\setminus A$, let \[ B_I=\{\beta_g|_I:g\in G\} \leq\operatorname{Homeo}^+(I) \tag{C.77.1} \] be its actual effective base image, with its induced compact-open and inverse topology. Retain every strip whose finite-endpoint characters are all zero, and every strip for which $B_I$ is abelian. Let $Z_{\mathrm{ab}}$ be their union with all lines over $A$ and the original circle. The restriction of the original loop to this closed set has a based contraction through its actual homeomorphisms, fixing the original circle and commuting with $Q$ on its interior part. The inverse family is jointly continuous. One compact family of original closed-disk maps controls all evaluations, including arbitrary accumulation of strips. For an abelian base image there are an actual increasing homeomorphism $b_I:I\to\mathbb R$ and a continuous source character $d_I:G\to\mathbb R$ such that \[ b_I(\beta_g(t))=b_I(t)+d_I(g),\qquad d_I(G)=\mathbb R. \tag{C.77.2} \] The prescribed base contraction is $b_I^{-1}(b_I(t)+r d_I(f_\tau))$, and each finite endpoint has the simultaneous displacement $r u_\tau(a)$. This includes abelian base strips with full-real endpoint-stabilizer character images. The exact restriction homomorphism is the map (C.76.4) with $Z_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in place of $Z$; no lifting through excluded strips is asserted. The set $Z$ of C.76 is contained in $Z_{\mathrm{ab}}$ by the actual translation comparison (C.75.4). There is also an exact description of the remaining character comparison. On a strip with nonabelian $B_I$, write $c:G\to V\subset\mathbb R^k$ for the vector of its finite-endpoint characters, $0\leq k\leq2$. Then \[ c(G_t)=V\quad(t\in I), \qquad T(g)(z,t)=(z+c(g),\beta_g(t)) \tag{C.77.3} \] defines a transitive action on the actual space $V\times I$. Let $L$ be the actual closed relative group used in C.76, and let $\mathscr P(L)$ be its Polish based path group. For each $t\in I$, endpoint evaluation gives an open surjection and the indicated homeomorphism \[ \begin{aligned} e_t:\mathscr P(L)&\longrightarrow V\times I,\\ e_t(\sigma)&=(c(\sigma(1)),\beta_{\sigma(1)}(t)),\\ \mathscr P(L)/J_t&\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }V\times I,\\ \sigma J_t&\longmapsto e_t(\sigma). \end{aligned} \tag{C.77.4} \] where $J_t=e_t^{-1}(0,t)$ is the actual stabilizer. Every sufficiently small compact target set has a compact preimage in any specified open path neighborhood whose image contains it. No continuous section, nor uniform compact preimage for targets escaping towards a strip endpoint, is inferred.

For every $n\geq1$ and every continuous based map $f:(S^n,*)\to(\mathscr C_Q,1)$, there is a continuous map $H:[0,1]\times S^n\to\mathscr C_Q$ satisfying \[ \begin{gathered} H_{0,\xi}=1,\qquad H_{1,\xi}=f_\xi,\qquad H_{r,*}=1.\\ \text{Consequently }\quad \pi_n(\mathscr C_Q,1)=0\quad(n\geq1). \end{gathered} \tag{C.80.2} \] Both evaluation families $H_{r,\xi}(x)$ and $H_{r,\xi}^{-1}(x)$ are jointly continuous on the original closed disk. Every original operator is retained. This proves the stated based homotopy groups, without asserting contractibility of the whole group or describing its components.

statement: Exact metric, compact-support, and finite-configuration comparisons for discrete operators — Let $O=\operatorname{int}\overline D$ be the actual open disk, let $d$ be a compatible metric on its closed disk, and let $Q\leq\operatorname{Homeo}(O)$ be closed, discrete, free and proper. Retain the actual relative centralizer \[ \mathscr C_Q= \{h\in\operatorname{Homeo}(\overline D): h|_{\partial\overline D}=\id, \ hq=qh\text{ on }O\text{ for every }q\in Q\} \tag{C.81.1} \] with compact-open convergence of maps and inverses. Assume that an actual subgroup $G\leq\mathscr C_Q$ is transitive on $O$. Write $N=O/Q$ and retain the original quotient covering $\pi:O\to N$. No extension of the operators $q$ to the circle is assumed. The following comparisons hold. The metric \[ \begin{split} d_Q(x,y)&=\sup_{q\in Q}d(qx,qy),\\ \rho(\pi x,\pi y)&=\inf_{q\in Q}d_Q(x,qy). \end{split} \tag{C.81.2} \] gives the original topology on $O$ and its quotient topology on $N$. The specified covering is locally isometric for these metrics and each fiber is uniformly discrete. Restriction embeds $\mathscr C_Q$ as a closed subgroup of the uniform $d_Q$-homeomorphisms commuting with $Q$, and is an isometry for the sum of the uniform map and inverse distances and the corresponding actual closed-disk distances. Every compact parameter family of equivariant interior homeomorphisms and their inverses, supported over one fixed compact subset of $N$, extends jointly by the identity to the original circle. In particular, every based sphere family in $\mathscr C_Q$ whose descents are supported in the interior of one compact connected subsurface $N_0\subset N$ with nonempty boundary has a based filling in $\mathscr C_Q$, retaining that quotient support and every original label. Here sphere dimension is any $n\geq1$. For finite $A\subset O$ with distinct quotient labels put $\mathscr C_Q(A)=\{h\in\mathscr C_Q:h|_A=\id\}$. For $x\notin QA$, the actual evaluation map is a locally trivial principal bundle \[ \mathscr C_Q(A\cup\{x\})\longrightarrow \mathscr C_Q(A)\xrightarrow{\ h\mapsto h(x)\ }O\setminus QA. \tag{C.81.3} \] Its source and fiber retain their original closed-disk topologies. Every inclusion $\mathscr C_Q(A)\hookrightarrow\mathscr C_Q$ induces an isomorphism on $\pi_n$ at $1$ for every $n\geq1$. When $N$ is noncompact, descent from the subgroup of actual lifts of compactly supported quotient isotopies is not continuous from its induced $\mathscr C_Q$ topology to the Whitney topology on the quotient homeomorphism group. The proof gives an explicit convergent sequence and one positive continuous majorant excluding all its descents. These are finite-configuration and fixed compact quotient-support comparisons. They do not provide a coherent infinite-configuration homotopy or a controlled fragmentation of every original family into compact quotient supports.

statement: A null lifted triangulation and its actual skeleton stabilizer — Retain the actual disk, discrete operator group, transitive relative subgroup, quotient covering and metrics of C.81. There is a locally finite triangulation $\mathcal T$ of $N=O/Q$ whose full lift $\widetilde{\mathcal T}$ through the original covering $\pi:O\to N$ has the following property: for every $\epsilon>0$, only finitely many lifted closed vertex stars have $d$-diameter at least $\epsilon$. In particular, this holds for the lifted closed triangles. Every such star is mapped injectively by $\pi$. Write $\Lambda=|\widetilde{\mathcal T}^{(1)}|$ for the actual lifted one-skeleton and set \[ \mathscr S_{Q,\Lambda} =\{h\in\mathscr C_Q:h|_\Lambda=\id\}. \tag{C.82.1} \] Choose one closed lifted triangle $D_\sigma$ for each two-simplex $\sigma$ of $\mathcal T$. Restriction and $Q$-equivariant pasting are mutually inverse topological group isomorphisms \[ \mathscr S_{Q,\Lambda} \ \cong\ \prod_{\sigma\in\mathcal T^{(2)}} \operatorname{Homeo}(D_\sigma\mathbin{\mathrm{rel}} \partial D_\sigma). \tag{C.82.2} \] Here $\mathcal T^{(2)}$ indexes the two-simplices, the product has the product topology, and the left side retains the original closed-disk topology of maps and inverses. Coordinatewise Alexander deformation gives a continuous contraction of this entire actual subgroup to $1$, fixing $1$ throughout. The conclusion concerns the pointwise skeleton stabilizer. A deformation of every original based sphere family in $\mathscr C_Q$ into that stabilizer, with joint original-boundary control, is not supplied by this statement or by the finite-label comparisons of C.81.

statement: An actual equivariant infinite-evaluation path without a closed-disk lift — There is an actual closed disk and a closed, discrete, free proper interior operator group $Q\cong\mathbb Z$ satisfying every hypothesis of C.81, including an actual transitive boundary-fixed subgroup of its centralizer, with the following property. For a specified ordered, locally finite, $Q$-invariant vertex set $V$, let $\mathscr E_V$ be the actual image of simultaneous labelled evaluation \[ \operatorname{ev}_V:\mathscr C_Q\longrightarrow\mathscr E_V. \tag{C.83.1} \] Give $\mathscr E_V$ the subspace topology of ordered coordinate convergence together with vague convergence of counting measures in the specified interior plane coordinate. The map (C.83.1) is continuous and onto. There is an explicit based null-homotopic loop in $\mathscr E_V$ which has no continuous lift to $\mathscr C_Q$ starting at $1$. Every point of that loop is the evaluation of a displayed actual boundary-fixed, $Q$-commuting homeomorphism. All original $Q$-labels are retained. The vertex set can be taken to be the full lift of a quotient triangulation having the null-star property of C.82. Thus, for these exact source and target topologies, infinite evaluation has neither the path-lifting property nor the Serre or Hurewicz fibration property. The proof does not assert a nontrivial homotopy class in the actual centralizer.

statement: The exact radial translation topology and a contractible monotone subspace — Retain the actual radial coordinate $j(z)=z/(1+\|z\|)$, its inverse, the original closed unit disk, and the operator $q=jT_{(1,0)}j^{-1}$ of C.83. Conjugation $h\mapsto j^{-1}hj$ is a topological group isomorphism from the actual relative centralizer $\mathscr C_Q$ onto the following explicitly topologized group $\mathscr P$. Its elements are plane homeomorphisms $F=(X_F,Y_F)$ commuting with $T_{(1,0)}$ and satisfying \[ \lim_{R\to\infty} \sup_{\substack{0\leq x\leq1\\ |y|\geq R}} \frac{\|F(x,y)-(x,y)\|}{|y|}=0. \tag{C.84.1} \] Every inverse satisfies the same condition. The exact topology on $\mathscr P$ is given by the finite metric \[ \begin{gathered} \|F-H\|_*= \sup_{\substack{0\leq x\leq1\\ y\in\mathbb R}} \frac{\|F(x,y)-H(x,y)\|}{1+|y|},\\ \delta_*(F,H)=\|F-H\|_*+\|F^{-1}-H^{-1}\|_*. \end{gathered} \tag{C.84.2} \] In (C.84.1) the limit is uniform over every compact family in the actual group. Let $\mathscr M\subset\mathscr P$ consist of those $F$ for which, at every $x$, $y\mapsto Y_F(x,y)$ is an increasing homeomorphism of $\mathbb R$. The proof gives an explicit continuous contraction of this entire subspace, fixing the identity, through the same subspace. Conjugating back through $j$ gives the contraction in the original closed-disk topology, preserving its circle and every original operator label. The inclusion $\mathscr M\hookrightarrow\mathscr P$ is proper, as witnessed by an explicit periodic core rotation below.

statement: A parametric cutoff and all positive homotopy groups in the radial cyclic model — Retain the exact coordinate $j$, original disk, operator $q=jT_{(1,0)}j^{-1}$, and topological group $\mathscr P$ of C.84. Moreover, $\mathcal C_R(F)\to F$ as $R\to\infty$ uniformly on compact families in the original closed-disk map-and-inverse topology. Consequently every based sphere family in the actual relative centralizer $\mathscr C_Q$ has a based filling there: \[ \pi_n(\mathscr C_Q,1)=0 \qquad(n\geq1). \tag{C.85.2} \] Every original boundary point and every original integer-translation label is retained. statement: The exact vanishing-displacement image and its compact-family topology — Retain all the actual hypotheses and maps of C.81: the original closed disk $\overline D$, its interior $O$, a compatible metric $d$ on $\overline D$, a closed discrete free proper operator group $Q$ on $O$, and a transitive subgroup of the original boundary-fixed centralizer $\mathscr C_Q$. Write $\pi:O\to N=O/Q$ and retain $d_Q(x,y)=\sup_{q\in Q}d(qx,qy)$. For an interior homeomorphism $h$ commuting with every actual $q$, put \[ \delta_h(\pi x)=d_Q(hx,x),\qquad \mathscr V_Q= \{h\in C_{\operatorname{Homeo}(O)}(Q): \delta_h\in C_0(N)\}. \tag{C.88.1} \] Here $C_0(N)$ means continuous real-valued functions whose absolute values are uniformly small off compact subsets of $N$. Then restriction and identity extension are mutually inverse topological group maps \[ \begin{aligned} R:\mathscr C_Q&\longrightarrow\mathscr V_Q, &R(a)&=a|_O,\\ E:\mathscr V_Q&\longrightarrow\mathscr C_Q, &E(h)|_O&=h,\quad E(h)|_{\partial\overline D}=\id . \end{aligned} \tag{C.88.2} \] The topology on $\mathscr V_Q$ is the sum of the uniform $d_Q$ distances of maps and inverses. These maps are isometries for the corresponding original closed-disk distances. Every member of $\mathscr V_Q$ and its inverse is automatically uniformly $d_Q$-continuous; no uniform-continuity assumption is added to (C.88.1). There is also an exact compact-parameter criterion. Let $P$ be a compact metric space and let $h_p$ be actual equivariant interior homeomorphisms such that $(p,x)\mapsto h_p(x)$ is continuous on $P\times O$. Their identity extensions form a continuous $P$-family of original closed-disk homeomorphisms and inverses precisely when \[ \forall\epsilon>0\ \exists K\subset N \text{ compact}\quad \sup_{\substack{p\in P\\ \pi x\notin K}} d_Q(h_p x,x)<\epsilon. \tag{C.88.3} \] In that case the inverse family has the same uniform vanishing property. Thus (C.88.3), with the actual interior maps retained, expresses the original boundary and compact-family requirements exactly. It supplies no cutoff deformation by itself.

statement: A global section for the actual compact skeleton image — Retain the actual hypotheses of C.81 and the null lifted triangulation of C.82. Write $\Lambda$ for its full one-skeleton and put \[ X=\Lambda\cup\partial\overline D . \tag{C.89.1} \] This is a compact connected subset of the original closed disk. Define $\mathscr B$ to be the following space of embeddings $b:X\to\overline D$, with uniform convergence on this actual compact domain: $b$ fixes the original circle, maps $\Lambda$ into $O$, and satisfies $b(qx)=q b(x)$ for every $x\in\Lambda$ and every original $q\in Q$. For each lifted closed triangle $\Delta$, its boundary image is positively oriented relative to the orientation of $\partial\Delta$, and the Jordan disk $D_b(\Delta)$ bounded by this image satisfies \[ \operatorname{int}D_b(\Delta)\cap b(X) =\varnothing . \tag{C.89.2} \] Then $\mathscr B$ is exactly the image of the original restriction map $\mathscr C_Q\to\operatorname{Emb}(X,\overline D)$. That map has a global continuous section $\mathfrak s:\mathscr B\to\mathscr C_Q$ with $\mathfrak s(\id_X)=\id$. Its construction retains all three labelled vertices of each representative triangle and every original deck operator, including orientation-reversing operators. If $\mathscr K=\mathscr S_{Q,\Lambda}$ is the pointwise stabilizer in C.82, the maps \[ \begin{aligned} \Phi:\mathscr B\times\mathscr K&\longrightarrow\mathscr C_Q, &\Phi(b,k)&=\mathfrak s(b)k,\\ \Psi:\mathscr C_Q&\longrightarrow\mathscr B\times\mathscr K, &\Psi(h)&=\bigl(h|_X,\mathfrak s(h|_X)^{-1}h\bigr) \end{aligned} \tag{C.89.3} \] are mutually inverse homeomorphisms of spaces, for the stated skeleton topology and the original map-and-inverse group topologies. The C.82 contraction of $\mathscr K$ supplies a strong deformation retraction of $\mathscr C_Q$ onto $\mathfrak s(\mathscr B)$. Thus the remaining based-family deformation can be expressed exactly on this compact equivariant skeleton image. No contraction of $\mathscr B$ is asserted here.

statement: Cocompact discrete operators in the original boundary topology — Retain all the actual disk, operator, transitivity, covering and topology hypotheses of C.81. For a compact quotient $N=O/Q$, every based sphere family in the original relative centralizer has a based filling in that same group: \[ \pi_n(\mathscr C_Q,1)=0\qquad(n\geq1). \tag{C.90.1} \] The filling fixes the original circle pointwise, commutes with each individual original $q\in Q$, and is continuous for both maps and inverses. The quotient may be nonorientable; in particular the torus and Klein-bottle cases are included. No boundary extension of an operator or of an interior conjugacy is required. More precisely, let $p\in N$, let $x\in O$ be a specified lift of $p$, and write \[ \mathscr C_Q(x)=\{h\in\mathscr C_Q:h(x)=x\},\qquad \mathscr H_p=\operatorname{Homeo}(N\mathbin{\mathrm{rel}}\{p\})^0. \tag{C.90.2} \] The superscript on $\mathscr H_p$ denotes its identity component with its compact-open group topology. Every based sphere family in $\mathscr C_Q(x)$ descends into $\mathscr H_p$. A single identity-fixed contraction of $\mathscr H_p$, lifted through the original covering from the identity, fills that sphere with its original endpoint maps retained. The inclusion $\mathscr C_Q(x)\hookrightarrow \mathscr C_Q$ is the positive-homotopy isomorphism of C.81, and transfers this filling to (C.90.1).

statement: A contraction of the whole cocompact original centralizer — Retain the actual hypotheses of C.81 and the compact quotient $N=O/Q$ of C.90. Thus $O=\operatorname{int}\overline D$ is the original open disk, $Q$ is closed, discrete, free and proper, and an actual subgroup of the boundary-fixed centralizer $\mathscr C_Q$ is transitive on $O$. Fix $x\in O$, put $p=\pi x$, and write $\mathscr F=\mathscr C_Q(x)$ and $\mathscr H_p=\operatorname{Homeo}(N\mathbin{\mathrm{rel}}\{p\})^0$. Give these groups their stated compact-open map-and-inverse topologies. There are exact topological group isomorphisms \[ \begin{aligned} D:\mathscr F&\longrightarrow\mathscr H_p, &D(h)(\pi z)&=\pi(hz),\\ L:\mathscr H_p&\longrightarrow\mathscr F, &L(b)|_{\partial\overline D}&=\id. \end{aligned} \tag{C.91.1} \] The interior restriction of $L(b)$ is exactly the unique lift of $b\pi$ that fixes $x$. In particular this identifies the entire actual point stabilizer, not only its identity component. The proof establishes that every one of its descents lies in the indicated pointed component. The evaluation map admits a continuous section $s:O\to\mathscr C_Q$ with $s(y)x=y$ and $s(x)=1$. Consequently the mutually inverse homeomorphisms \[ \begin{aligned} \Phi:O\times\mathscr F&\longrightarrow\mathscr C_Q, &\Phi(y,k)&=s(y)k,\\ \Psi:\mathscr C_Q&\longrightarrow O\times\mathscr F, &\Psi(h)&=(hx,s(hx)^{-1}h) \end{aligned} \tag{C.91.2} \] give an identity-fixed contraction of the whole original $\mathscr C_Q$. All maps in the contraction fix the original circle and commute with every individual original $q\in Q$. The assertion includes the torus, Klein bottle, and all the other compact quotient surfaces permitted by these data.

statement: Arbitrary pointed descents and the exact original lift topology — Retain all the actual data of C.81: the original closed disk $\overline D$, its interior $O$, the compatible closed-disk metric $d$, the closed discrete free proper group $Q$ of operators on $O$, the boundary-fixed centralizer $\mathscr C_Q$ with a transitive actual subgroup, and the specified quotient covering $\pi:O\to N=O/Q$. The quotient $N$ is allowed to be noncompact throughout this note. Fix $x\in O$, put $p=\pi x$, and set $\mathscr F=\mathscr C_Q(x)$. Write $\mathscr I_p$ for the identity path component of $\operatorname{Homeo}(N\mathbin{\mathrm{rel}}\{p\})$ in the compact-open topology of maps and inverses. Thus a path in this definition has jointly continuous maps and inverses on $[0,1]\times N$. Every member of the entire original $\mathscr F$ descends into $\mathscr I_p$. Below we prove this assertion without assuming component membership upstairs. We also identify its exact image inside $\mathscr I_p$, with inverse maps and both relevant topologies. The original compact-quotient contraction C.91 remains unchanged. More precisely, let $\lambda(b)$ be the unique lift of $b\pi$ fixing $x$ for $b\in\mathscr I_p$. The image of $D$ is exactly the subgroup $\mathscr B_p$ defined by $\delta_b(\pi z)=d_Q(\lambda(b)z,z)\in C_0(N)$. Descent and extension of this lift are inverse group maps and are isometric for the original sum metric and the lifted sum metric in (C.92.15). On a compact parameter space their exact continuity criterion is the uniform tail (C.92.17). The explicit noncompact example (C.92.18)--(C.92.21) gives a sequence in this exact image converging in the quotient compact-open topology whose pointed lifts stay more than $2/5$ from the identity in the original metric.

statement: Finite subgroups of completed surface orbifold groups, including reflections — Every finite subgroup of $\widehat E$ is conjugate to a finite subgroup of $E$. These finite subgroups are cyclic rotation groups or dihedral groups, with a single reflection included as the dihedral case of order two.

statement: The exact profinite fixed subgroup of a section — Let $s:H\to E_H$ be a nontrivial discrete section. Its fixed subgroup $P^{s(H)}=C_P(s(H))$ is trivial when $s(H)$ contains a nontrivial rotation. For a reflection $s(H)=\langle t\rangle$, it is $1$ for a noncompact real component and is the closure of the primitive oval subgroup, isomorphic to $\widehat\Z$, for a compact real component. The same assertions hold for every profinite section by D.3.

statement: A well-defined transfer of the geometric rotation invariant — For a realized $E$, its rotation invariant on finite-order elements transfers uniquely to the torsion of $\widehat E$ by conjugating each torsion element into $E$. This assertion uses the orientation module, so that conjugation by an orientation-reversing element acts by $-1$ on its values. Its values embed canonically in $\widehat T\otimes_{\Z}\Q/\Z$, where $\widehat T=T\otimes_{\Z}\widehat\Z$.

statement: Equivariance of the profinite rotation invariant — Let $E$ be the lift group of a finite action on an orientable hyperbolic surface of finite type, and put $P=\widehat\pi\triangleleft\widehat E$. Every automorphism $\alpha$ of $\widehat E$ preserving $P$ and its indexed peripheral structure satisfies \[ \mu_{\widehat E}(\alpha(u))=\alpha_T\bigl(\mu_{\widehat E}(u)\bigr) \qquad (u\in\widehat E\text{ of finite order}). \] Here $\alpha_T$ is the induced automorphism of the orientation line $\widehat T$ defined in A.2, and $\mu_{\widehat E}$ is the invariant of D.6. The assertion holds for compact and noncompact surfaces, and for actions containing orientation-reversing elements.

statement: The nonsolvable discrete possibilities in genus at most two — A nonsolvable finite subgroup of the extended mapping class group of a punctured orientable surface of genus at most two is realized on a sphere and has group $A_5$ or $A_5\times C_2$. Its puncture set is invariant under the corresponding icosahedral action. In particular it has at least twelve punctures. This classification does not assert the absence of additional nonsolvable finite subgroups in completions for all larger puncture numbers.

statement: Finite torsion in the odd-prime normalized pro-$p$ centralizer — Let $p$ be odd, let $F^{(p)}$ be the free pro-$p$ group on $x,y$, and define $GT_{0,p}$ by the normalized automorphisms \[ F_{\lambda,f}(x)=x^\lambda,\qquad F_{\lambda,f}(y)=f^{-1}y^\lambda f, \quad \lambda\in\Z_p^\times,\quad f\in(F^{(p)})', \] satisfying the two-cycle and three-cycle equations. Every finite subgroup of $GT_{0,p}$ is cyclic of order dividing $p-1$. There is a subgroup of order $p-1$, and every finite subgroup is conjugate in $GT_{0,p}$ to a subgroup of it. For $p\geq5$ this supplies finite loop-preserving outer automorphism groups which are not conjugate to geometric groups of the three-punctured sphere.

statement: Executed finite checks and their exact scope — The program \texttt{code/root/finite\_checks.py} verifies the two-cycle and three-cycle equations in every Heisenberg group $H(\F_p)$ for $p=5,7,11$ and every $\lambda\in\F_p^\times$, using \[ f(a,b)=[a,b]^{(\lambda^2-1)/24},\qquad m=(\lambda-1)/2. \] In particular it verifies an order-four normalized automorphism at $(p,\lambda\bmod p)=(5,2)$ and an order-three one at $(7,2)$. The multipliers of the corresponding infinite finite-order subgroups are Teichm\"uller lifts of these residues; the integer $2\in\Z_5^\times$ itself has infinite order. D.10, not the finite checks alone, proves the existence of compatible infinite pro-$p$ lifts.

statement: A precise fixed-set formula for every actual action — Let $A$ be a group, $J\leq A$, and $G\leq A$ a finite subgroup. statement: The unmarked pro-$p$ extension statement for punctured surfaces — A finitely generated torsion-free pro-$p$ group $\mathcal E$ containing an open free pro-$p$ group $P$ of rank $r$ is free pro-$p$. Its rank is \[ 1+\frac{r-1}{[\mathcal E:P]}. \] In particular the displayed quantity is an integer. This proves the underlying-group assertion for punctured pro-$p$ surfaces, without identifying the peripheral system. More generally, every torsion-free profinite group with an open normal pro-$p$ subgroup is itself pro-$p$. Thus D.19--D.20 apply to arbitrary finite-quotient extensions of their pro-$p$ kernels; the quotient is forced to be a $p$-group.

statement: Order-preserving lifting and conjugacy in the full shadow system — Let $\mathcal I$ be the cofiltered poset of isolated finite-index normal subgroups $N\unlhd B_3$ contained in the pure braid group $PB_3$, and put $Q_N=GT(N)$. The finite groups and their reduction homomorphisms $R_{N,H}:Q_N\to Q_H$ for $N\subseteq H$ are those of \cite[Proposition 3.14, Theorem 5.2 and Proposition 5.5]{A-DGShadows}. We use the continuous isomorphism \[ \Psi:GT_0\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\varprojlim_{N\in\mathcal I}Q_N, \qquad (\lambda,f)\longmapsto \bigl([ (\lambda-1)/2,f]_N\bigr)_N. \] For a positive integer $d$, write $T_d(Q)=\{q\in Q:q^d=1\}$. For each $H\in\mathcal I$, the image of $T_d(GT_0)$ in $Q_H$ is exactly \[ \bigcap_{\substack{N\in\mathcal I\\N\subseteq H}} R_{N,H}\bigl(T_d(Q_N)\bigr). \tag{D.23a} \] An element of order exactly $d$ in this intersection has a lift of order exactly $d$. Every element of order exactly $d$ in $GT_0$ has an image of order exactly $d$ at some isolated level. For $a,b\in GT_0$, conjugacy in $GT_0$ is equivalent to conjugacy of $\Psi(a)_N$ and $\Psi(b)_N$ in every $Q_N$.

statement: All-prime dihedral compatibility and the multiplier-one obstruction — The inverse limit $D$ over all the dihedral levels of D.24 has the following explicit isomorphism of profinite groups: \[ D\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \left(\prod_{p\text{ odd}}\operatorname{Aff}(\Z_p)\right) \times H_2. \tag{D.25a} \] There is a canonical continuous homomorphism $GT_0\to D$. The group $D$ contains an element of every prime order. In particular, imposing order three throughout this entire dihedral system still permits a multiplier whose $7$-adic coordinate is a primitive cube root and whose other prime coordinates are $1$. Put $F=\widehat F_2=\langle x,y\rangle$ and define the continuous epimorphism and its closed kernel by \[ \kappa:F\longrightarrow\prod_pF_2^{(p)},\qquad R=\ker\kappa. \] Write $\lambda:GT_0\to\widehat\Z^\times$ for the multiplier. For every integer $d\geq2$, the elements $a\in\ker\lambda$ with $a^d=1$ correspond exactly to the following elements $f\in R$. The continuous endomorphism \[ \alpha_f:F\to F,\qquad x\mapsto x,\quad y\mapsto f^{-1}yf \] must be an automorphism and satisfy \[ \theta(f)f=1,\qquad \tau^2(f)\tau(f)f=1,\qquad \prod_{j=0}^{d-1}\alpha_f^{j}(f)=1, \tag{D.25b} \] where the product is in increasing order of $j$, $\theta(x)=y$, $\theta(y)=x$, $\tau(x)=y$, and $\tau(y)=(xy)^{-1}$. Every such finite-order element has identity image in $D$. The kernel $R$ itself maps onto the explicit perfect group $A_5$ used in D.24. The finite-order solutions of (D.25b) in the stated automorphism domain are exactly $f=1$, by D.32's subsequent full fixed-subgroup argument. Thus the nontrivial prime-order points of the dihedral inverse limit exhibited here do not lift with that order to $GT_0$ when the prime is odd.

Each such section $S$ satisfies \[ H^1(C_F(S),\F_3)=0. \tag{D.48a} \] The normalizer in $E_a$ of the torus cusp $L=\overline{\langle[x,y]\rangle}$ is torsion-free. If $v$ is any element of this normalizer projecting to the prescribed generator $a$, and \[ v[x,y]v^{-1}=[x,y]^\lambda,\qquad v^3=[x,y]^\kappa , \] then its $3$-adic coordinate satisfies $\kappa_3\in\Z_3^\times$.

statement: The standard centralizer and the two-element conjugator fibres — Let $P$ be the full pure three-cusp group of D.32 and $\delta(x)=x^{-1}$, $\delta(y)=y^{-1}$. Its full centralizer and normalizer are \[ C_P(\delta)=N_P(\langle\delta\rangle) =\langle\delta\rangle. \tag{D.49a} \] Define the actual conjugacy orbits \[ \mathcal O_P=\{\beta\delta\beta^{-1}:\beta\in P\}, \qquad \mathcal O_{GT_0}=\{\beta\delta\beta^{-1}:\beta\in GT_0\}. \] Every fibre of $P\to\mathcal O_P$ is exactly the right coset $\{\beta,\beta\delta\}$, and \[ \mathcal O_{GT_0} =\mathcal O_P\cap GT_0. \tag{D.49b} \] For $\alpha\in\mathcal O_P$, its two conjugators have the exact normalized formulas \[ \begin{array}{ll} x\mapsto x^\mu,& y\mapsto h y^\mu h^{-1},\\ x\mapsto x^{-\mu},& y\mapsto h y^{-\mu}h^{-1}, \end{array} \qquad \mu\in\widehat\Z^\times,\quad h\in F'. \tag{D.49c} \] Here $h$ is unique, and the unordered pair $\{\mu,-\mu\}$ is unique. In D.35's solution space, a choice $(\mu,h,u)$ therefore gives all the solutions over $\alpha$ as \[ (\mu,h,u(xy)^a),\qquad (-\mu,h,x^{-\mu}u(xy)^a),\qquad a\in\widehat\Z. \tag{D.49d} \] These assertions concern the specified orbit map; they do not assert that it contains every full pure or $GT_0$ involution.

statement: The finite two-subgroups of the full punctured-torus group — Let $T=\Out_{\rm lac}(\widehat F(x,y); \overline{\langle[x,y]\rangle})$ be the full once-punctured-torus loop-outer group. The possible abstract isomorphism types of its finite $2$-subgroups are exactly \[ 1,\quad C_2,\quad C_4,\quad C_2\times C_2,\quad D_8, \tag{D.50a} \] where $D_8$ has order eight. All five types occur. For a subgroup of type $C_2\times C_2$ or $D_8$, the full multiplier takes its values in the globally constant signs $\{1,-1\}\subset\widehat\Z^\times$. In $C_2\times C_2$ there is one positive involution and two negative involutions. In $D_8$ the rotation subgroup has multiplier $1$ and the four reflections have multiplier $-1$. For an arbitrary cyclic subgroup of order four, a generator $a$ satisfies the already proved restrictions \[ \lambda(a)^2=1,\qquad \lambda(a)_2=1, \qquad \lambda(a^2)=1. \tag{D.50b} \] The abstract classification (D.50a) does not establish conjugacy of arbitrary such subgroups, or replace (D.50b) by a global multiplier determination.

statement: The second index-three kernel and its three peripheral normalizers — Let $a$ have order three in the full punctured-torus loop-outer group, put $F=\widehat F(x,y)$, $c=[x,y]$, and let $E$ be its centre-free extension. Besides $F$, there is exactly one other torsion-free normal subgroup $U$ of index three in $E$. Write $V=F\cap U$. Then \[ \begin{gathered} [F:V]=[U:V]=3,\qquad E/V\cong C_3^2,\\ V=\widehat{\pi_1(S_{1,3})},\qquad U\ \hbox{is projective},\qquad U^{(3)}\cong\widehat F^{(3)}_2 . \end{gathered} \tag{D.51a} \] The cusp normalizer $N=N_E(\langle c\rangle)$ is contained in $U$. The three cusp subgroups $L_0,L_1,L_2$ of the displayed degree-three cover have normalizers $N_i=N_U(L_i)$ with the exact sequences \[ 1\longrightarrow L_i \longrightarrow N_i \longrightarrow U/V\longrightarrow1. \tag{D.51b} \] They are three distinct $U$-conjugacy classes, cyclically permuted by $E/U$. All have the given multiplier $\lambda$ under the same generator label in $U/V$. For a prime $q\ne3$ at which $\lambda_q$ is a nonidentity cube root of unity, the $U/V$-character multiplicities of $H_1(V,\Q_q)$, ordered as $(1,\lambda_q,\lambda_q^2)$, are exactly one of \[ (1,3,0),\qquad (0,2,2). \tag{D.51c} \] Correspondingly $U^{(q)}$ is free pro-$q$ of rank one or zero. These are constraints on the actual subgroup $U$; they do not identify it with a full free profinite group.

statement: An abstract allowed list for every finite full torus subgroup — Let $T$ be the full once-punctured-torus loop-outer group of D.50. Every finite subgroup of $T$ has one of the following twelve abstract types: \[ \begin{gathered} 1,\ C_2,\ C_3,\ C_4,\ C_2\times C_2,\ C_6,\ S_3,\ D_8,\\ C_{12},\ D_{12},\ \operatorname{Dic}_{12},\ D_{24}. \end{gathered} \tag{D.52a} \] Here $D_{2n}$ has order $2n$, and $\operatorname{Dic}_{12}=C_3\rtimes C_4$, with a generator of $C_4$ inverting $C_3$. The nine types obtained by omitting $C_{12},\operatorname{Dic}_{12},D_{24}$ all occur. Occurrence of those three remaining types is not determined by this allowed list. The subsequent full covering arguments in D.54--D.55 exclude all three. Every subgroup of type $S_3,D_{12}$ or $D_{24}$ has the global usual reflection multiplier: rotations have multiplier $1$ and reflections have multiplier $-1$. In a subgroup of type $\operatorname{Dic}_{12}$, the subgroup of order three has multiplier $1$, and every generator $b$ of a cyclic subgroup of order four satisfies \[ \lambda(b)^2=1,\qquad \lambda(b)_2=1,\qquad\lambda(b)_3=-1. \tag{D.52b} \] For a subgroup of type $C_{12}$, its order-four generator instead has $\lambda(b)_2=\lambda(b)_3=1$, and still has $\lambda(b)^2=1$. These restrictions retain the unresolved cyclic order-three and order-four multiplier questions.

statement: No fixed character for a cubic torus action — Let $a$ have order three in the full once-punctured-torus loop-outer group. For every prime $q\ne3$, it fixes no nonzero continuous character \[ \chi:F\longrightarrow C_q, \qquad F=\widehat F(x,y). \tag{D.54a} \] Consequently the reduction of $A_q(a)$ modulo $q$ has no eigenvalue one. In particular, $A_2$ is injective on every finite subgroup of the full torus group. The allowed list of D.52 loses $C_{12}$ and $D_{24}$. statement: Full primary faithfulness and the nine finite torus types — Every positive involution $b$ in the full once-punctured-torus loop-outer group has \[ A_p(b)=-I \quad\text{for every prime }p. \tag{D.55a} \] Consequently, for each prime $p$, the actual homology map $A_p$ is injective on every finite subgroup of that group. The possible finite abstract subgroup types are exactly the following nine, all realized: \[ 1,\ C_2,\ C_3,\ C_4,\ C_2\times C_2,\ C_6,\ S_3,\ D_8,\ D_{12}. \tag{D.55b} \] The groups $D_8,D_{12}$ have orders eight and twelve respectively. For an arbitrary order-four element $a$, \[ A_p(a)^2=-I\quad\text{for every }p. \tag{D.55c} \] At a negative multiplier coordinate $q$ it is necessarily a scalar matrix $i_q I$ or $-i_q I$, where $i_q^2=-1$ in $\Q_q$; thus $q\equiv1\pmod4$. Together with (D.54b), this retains the precise scalar cubic and quartic multiplier cases. The abstract classification (D.55b) does not settle those scalar cases or the conjugacy of arbitrary finite subgroups.

statement: The prime sections of a cyclic-six torus action — Let $a$ have order six in the full once-punctured-torus loop-outer group of $F=\widehat F(x,y)$, and let \[ E=\{(\phi,j)\in\operatorname{Aut}(F)\times C_6: [\phi]=a^j\} \tag{D.56a} \] be its centre-free extension, with kernel identified with $F$ by the inner-automorphism map. There are exactly three $F$-conjugacy classes of order-two sections over $\langle a^3\rangle$ and exactly two $F$-conjugacy classes of order-three sections over $\langle a^2\rangle$. Conjugation by an element with quotient label $a^2$ cycles the three former classes; conjugation by an element with quotient label $a^3$ exchanges the two latter classes. Consequently $E$ has exactly one conjugacy class of subgroups of order two and one of order three, and these are its only nontrivial finite subgroup types. In particular the full extension (D.56a) does not split, and $a$ has no finite-order representative in $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$. For each prime section $S$ of order $p=2$ or $3$, \[ N_E(S)=C_F(S)\times S, \qquad H^1(C_F(S),\F_p)=0. \tag{D.56b} \] The assertions concern these specified extension and section maps; they do not identify $E$ with a free profinite product.

statement: The negative cusp section and its fixed homology line — Let $b$ be a negative involution in the full once-punctured-torus loop-outer group, let $F=\widehat F(x,y)$ and $c=[x,y]$, and choose a cusp reflection $v$ in its centre-free extension $E$. Thus \[ E=F\rtimes\langle v\rangle,\qquad v^2=1,\qquad vcv^{-1}=c^{-1}. \] Put $\alpha=\operatorname{Inn}(v)|_F$, $C=C_F(v)$, and \[ M=H_1(F,\widehat\Z),\qquad M^+=\ker(\alpha_*-I:M\to M). \] Then the cusp section is specifically the class with \[ H^1(C,\F_2)=0,\qquad C\subseteq\overline{[F,F]}. \tag{D.59a} \] For every actual transporter $g$ supplied by D.58, \[ gvg^{-1}=cv, \tag{D.59b} \] its homology class is a generator of the full fixed line: \[ \widehat\Z\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }M^+,\qquad t\longmapsto t[g]. \tag{D.59c} \] This line is a direct summand of $M$. More precisely, let $m\geq3$ be odd and let $\chi:F\to C_m$ be any surjective continuous $\alpha$-invariant character. Extend it to $\widetilde\chi:E\to C_m$ by $\widetilde\chi(v)=0$, and put $F_m=\ker\chi$, $E_m=\ker\widetilde\chi$. Then \[ C\subset F_m,\qquad \chi(g)\text{ generates }C_m,\qquad E_m=F_m\rtimes\langle v\rangle . \tag{D.59d} \] The $m$ cusp-dihedral edges form one cycle on the $m$ $F_m$-section classes above the original cusp class. Their fixed groups are conjugates of the same full group $C$. The complete section counts in this cover are \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \alpha_*\bmod2& \text{cusp classes in }E_m& \text{other classes in }E_m\\ \hline I&m\text{, each with }H^1(-,\F_2)=0& 1\text{, with }\dim H^1(-,\F_2)=1\\ \ne I&m\text{, each with }H^1(-,\F_2)=0&0 . \end{array} \tag{D.59e} \] In the first row, if $D=C_F(w)$ is the fixed group of the other full section class, its actual homology-image map is surjective: \[ D\longrightarrow M^+ . \tag{D.59f} \] These statements specify full subgroup cohomology and the indicated ambient homology maps. They make no identification of $C$ with the trivial group, of $D$ with a procyclic group, or of $g$ with a member of a full free profinite basis.

statement: The exact torsion quotient of a negative torus extension — Use D.59's notation \[ E=F\rtimes\langle v\rangle,\quad F=\widehat F(x,y), \quad c=[x,y],\quad v^2=1,\quad \alpha=\operatorname{Inn}(v)|_F,\quad M=F^{\rm ab}, \] and choose an actual transporter $g$ with $gvg^{-1}=cv$. For a subset of a profinite group, double angle brackets below mean its closed normal closure in the specified ambient group. There are exact continuous quotient identifications \[ \begin{split} E/\langle\!\langle v\rangle\!\rangle_E &\ \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\ M/(\alpha_*-I)M,\\ E/\langle\!\langle\operatorname{Tor}(E)\rangle\!\rangle_E &\ \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\ \widehat\Z , \end{split} \tag{D.60a} \] where $\operatorname{Tor}(E)$ is the set of finite-order elements. More explicitly, \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} A_2\bmod2& E/\langle\!\langle v\rangle\!\rangle_E& \chi(g)\\ \hline I&\widehat\Z\times C_2&1\\ \ne I&\widehat\Z&2 . \end{array} \tag{D.60b} \] Here $\chi:E\to\widehat\Z$ is the second quotient in (D.60a), with the normalization specified in the proof. Its restriction to $F$ is onto. It has a continuous section whose image lies in $F$, so \[ E=\langle\!\langle\operatorname{Tor}(E)\rangle\!\rangle_E \rtimes s(\widehat\Z). \tag{D.60c} \] In the first row, let $w$ represent the other full section class. One can choose that section $s$ inside $C_F(w)$, and the resulting map \[ \widehat\Z\times C_2\longrightarrow E,\qquad (t,\epsilon)\longmapsto s(t)w^\epsilon \tag{D.60d} \] is a continuous embedding. statement: Full generation and exact negative conjugator equations — Put $F=\widehat F(x,y)$ and $c=[x,y]$. Every closed subgroup $J\leq F$ satisfying $c\in\overline{[J,J]}$ is $F$ itself. Consequently every continuous endomorphism of $F$ carrying $c$ to a conjugate of $c^\mu$, with $\mu\in\widehat\Z^\times$, is an automorphism. Let $b$ be any negative full once-punctured-torus outer involution, with the specified extension \[ E=F\rtimes\langle v\rangle,\quad v^2=1,\quad vcv^{-1}=c^{-1}. \] Let $A_2$ be its action on $H_1(F,\Z_2)$. Set $v_i=c^iv$ and $\alpha_i=\operatorname{Inn}(v_i)|_F$, for $i=0,1$. On a separate free profinite group $F_0=\widehat F(X,Y)$, with $c_0=[X,Y]$, use the two standard actual negative involutions \[ \begin{array}{c|cc} &X&Y\\ \hline \beta_0&YXY^{-1}&Y^{-1}\\ \beta_1&Y&X . \end{array} \tag{D.61a} \] For $j=0,1$, let $\mathcal T_j(b)$ be the space of peripheral outer isomorphisms $[\phi]:F_0\to F$ conjugating $[\beta_j]$ to $b$. The peripheral requirement is $\phi(c_0)\sim_F c^\mu$ for a full unit $\mu$. Identifying $F_0$ with $F$ by $X\mapsto x$, $Y\mapsto y$ identifies this with the usual outer conjugator space. For $A_2\bmod2=I$, define \[ \begin{split} \mathcal S_{0,i}=\{(\mu,h,w):\ &\mu\in\widehat\Z^\times,\ h\in F,\quad w^2=1,\ w\in E\setminus F,\\ &w\text{ belongs to the other full section class},\\ &[h,w]=1,\quad [h,v_i]=c^\mu\}. \end{split} \tag{D.61b} \] Here \emph{other} means the class distinct from the common cusp-reflection class of D.58. There is a continuous bijection, with continuous inverse, \[ \mathcal S_{0,0}\sqcup\mathcal S_{0,1} \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\mathcal T_0(b),\qquad (\mu,h,w)\longmapsto [\,X\mapsto h,\ Y\mapsto v_iw\,]. \tag{D.61c} \] For $A_2\bmod2\ne I$, define \[ \mathcal S_{1,i} =\{(\mu,f)\in\widehat\Z^\times\times F: [f,\alpha_i(f)]=c^\mu\}. \tag{D.61d} \] The corresponding continuous bijection is \[ \mathcal S_{1,0}\sqcup\mathcal S_{1,1} \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\mathcal T_1(b),\qquad (\mu,f)\longmapsto [\,X\mapsto f,\ Y\mapsto\alpha_i(f)\,]. \tag{D.61e} \] Equivalently, writing $z=fv_i$, the last equation is \[ z\in E\setminus F,\qquad [z^2,v_i]=c^\mu. \tag{D.61f} \] The two basis images are then $zv_i,v_iz$. Thus no separate generation condition occurs in either parameter space. The equations and their outer conjugator spaces are identified exactly; nonemptiness for an arbitrary $b$ remains unproved.

statement: Primitive homology centralizers and the exact cusp-transporter root test — Let $F=\widehat F(x,y)$ and let $g\in F$ have primitive abelianization: there is a continuous homomorphism $\rho:F\to\widehat\Z$ with $\rho(g)=1$. Then, for every nonzero integer $n$, \[ C_F(g^n)=\overline{\langle g\rangle}\cong\widehat\Z, \qquad N_F(\overline{\langle g\rangle}) =\overline{\langle g\rangle}. \tag{D.62a} \] This conclusion uses homology primitivity; it does not require a free basis containing $g$. Now use the exact negative torus extension of D.58--D.61: \[ \begin{gathered} E=F\rtimes\langle v\rangle,\qquad v^2=1,\qquad \alpha=\operatorname{Inn}(v)|_F,\qquad c=[x,y],\qquad \alpha(c)=c^{-1},\\ C=C_F(v),\qquad gvg^{-1}=cv. \end{gathered} \tag{D.62b} \] D.59 supplies the required primitive abelianization of this $g$ and the exact inclusion $C\subseteq\overline{F'}$. For every $g'\in gC$, the following two conditions are equivalent: \[ \begin{split} &\alpha(g')\text{ is conjugate to }g'\text{ in }F;\\ &C_E(g')\text{ contains an element outside }F. \end{split} \tag{D.62c} \] Their consequences and converse maps are exact: \begin{enumerate} \item In the two-section-class case of D.58, they are equivalent to the existence of an involution $w\in E\setminus F$ centralizing $g'$. That involution is unique, belongs to the other section class, and \[ C_E(g')=\overline{\langle g'\rangle}\times\langle w\rangle. \tag{D.62d} \] The maps \[ X\longmapsto g',\qquad Y\longmapsto vw,\qquad v_0\longmapsto v \tag{D.62e} \] give a full isomorphism from the two-class standard extension in D.61 to $E$, preserving the quotient labels and carrying $[X,Y]$ to $c$. \item In the one-section-class case of D.58, they are equivalent to the existence of $z\in E\setminus F$ with $z^2=g'$. This root is unique, and \[ C_E(g')=\overline{\langle z\rangle}\cong\widehat\Z, \qquad F\cap C_E(g')=\overline{\langle z^2\rangle} =\overline{\langle g'\rangle}. \tag{D.62f} \] The maps \[ X\longmapsto zv,\qquad Y\longmapsto vz,\qquad v_0\longmapsto v \tag{D.62g} \] give the corresponding full isomorphism from the one-class standard extension, with the same exact peripheral and quotient labels. \end{enumerate} Thus the multiplier-one, $v_0\mapsto v$ portion of the D.61 conjugator problem is exactly the existence of a member $g'\in gC$ satisfying (D.62c). The explicit continuation (D.62q)--(D.62w) treats every full unit multiplier and both actual reflection labels, and gives the same criterion for the entire D.61 conjugator space. Neither equivalence asserts that its required conjugacy occurs.
