statement: The exact homology characters of a negative torus centralizer — Let $\Omega$ be the full once-punctured-torus peripheral outer group, and let $b\in\Omega$ be a negative involution. Keep the actual extension and peripheral labels of D.59--D.62: \[ \begin{gathered} F=\widehat F(x,y),\quad c=[x,y],\quad E=F\rtimes\langle v\rangle,\quad \alpha=\operatorname{Inn}(v)|_F,\quad v^2=1,\quad \alpha(c)=c^{-1},\\ M=F_{\rm ab},\quad A=\alpha_*,\quad C=C_F(v),\quad gvg^{-1}=cv,\quad M^+=\ker(A-I)=\widehat\Z[g]. \end{gathered} \tag{D.63a} \] In particular, D.59 says that $[g]$ is primitive and $C\subseteq\overline{F'}$. Put $Z_b=C_\Omega(b)$. There are actual continuous characters \[ \sigma:Z_b\longrightarrow\{1,-1\},\qquad \lambda:Z_b\longrightarrow\widehat\Z^\times \tag{D.63b} \] such that $\lambda$ is the peripheral multiplier, $\beta_*[g]=\sigma(\beta)[g]$, and the full homology matrix of every $\beta\in Z_b$ is exactly \[ \rho(\beta)= \frac{\sigma(\beta)}2 \bigl((1+\lambda(\beta))I+(1-\lambda(\beta))A\bigr) \quad\text{in }\operatorname{GL}_2(\widehat\Z). \tag{D.63c} \] Both half-coefficients in this formula belong to $\widehat\Z$: a full unit is odd at two, and two is invertible at every odd prime. In particular, \[ \lambda(\beta)=1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \rho(\beta)=\sigma(\beta)I. \tag{D.63d} \] Write \[ \begin{split} \Xi_b&=\{(\sigma(\beta),\lambda(\beta)):\beta\in Z_b\},\\ I_b&=Z_b\cap\ker\bigl(\Omega\longrightarrow \operatorname{GL}_2(\widehat\Z)\bigr). \end{split} \] The exact character sequence is \[ 1\longrightarrow I_b\longrightarrow Z_b \xrightarrow{\,(\sigma,\lambda)\,}\Xi_b \longrightarrow1. \tag{D.63e} \] Its kernel has the following description by actual automorphisms, with inverse maps given in the proof: \[ I_b\ \cong\ J_b:= \{\psi\in\operatorname{Aut}(F): \psi(c)=c,\ \psi\alpha=\alpha\psi\}. \tag{D.63f} \] Every member of $J_b$ automatically acts trivially on $M$. The group $I_b$ is torsion-free. This description does not assert that $I_b$ is trivial, or that $\Xi_b$ is the whole product in (D.63b). Every finite subgroup $K\leq Z_b$ has the exact faithful homology embedding \[ K\ \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\ \{I,-I,A_2,-A_2\}\cong C_2\times C_2, \qquad \beta\longmapsto \rho_2(\beta). \tag{D.63g} \] Here $A_2$ is the original dyadic involution matrix. Thus its possible abstract types are $1,C_2,C_2^2$; a finite subgroup containing $b$ has order two or four. This bound makes no assertion that a four-element subgroup occurs for every $b$.

statement: The unique full branch lift and its exact source coset — Keep the actual eight-point configuration $\mathcal P_8$ and involution $\mathsf r$ of F.12--17. Write \[ \begin{split} P_{10}^{\dagger} &=\widehat{P\Gamma}(\mathbf P^1;\mathcal P_8,a_+,a_-),\\ P_8&=\widehat{P\Gamma}(\mathbf P^1;\mathcal P_8),\\ f:P_{10}^{\dagger}&\longrightarrow P_8,\qquad \mathcal J=\ker f,\\ C^\dagger&=C_{P_{10}^{\dagger}}(\mathsf r^\dagger), \qquad C_8=C_{P_8}(\mathsf r). \end{split} \tag{F.18.1} \] Here $f$ forgets exactly the two named added points. The branch-permutation character $\epsilon:C_8\twoheadrightarrow C_2$ is defined by the actual decorated quotient of $\mathsf r$. Then \[ f:C^\dagger\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }C_8^+ :=\ker\epsilon,\qquad C_{\mathcal J}(\mathsf r^\dagger)=1 \tag{F.18.2} \] are an isomorphism of profinite groups and its exact kernel assertion. For the action $R^\dagger$ on $\mathcal J$ by $\mathsf r^\dagger$, the full continuous cocycles \[ Z^1(R^\dagger,\mathcal J) =\{\delta\in\mathcal J:\delta R^\dagger(\delta)=1\} \tag{F.18.3} \] have precisely two $\mathcal J$-conjugacy classes. Every order-two section has trivial centralizer in $\mathcal J$. In particular the map \[ b\longmapsto b^{-1}R^\dagger(b) \tag{F.18.4} \] is a homeomorphism from $\mathcal J$ onto the coboundary class. More generally, for $k\in P_{10}^{\dagger}$ with $f(k)\in C_8$, the class of $k^{-1}R^\dagger(k)$ is the class labelled $\epsilon(f(k))$. The original residual group $\mathcal E$ of F.12 has a unique full centralizing branch lift \[ \ell:\mathcal E\longrightarrow C^\dagger,\qquad f\ell=\widehat\phi|_{\mathcal E}. \tag{F.18.5} \] It is continuous and injective. This includes the proof that its branch character is zero; no ordered drilling is assumed in advance. Here is the exact remaining comparison to the rational drilling of F.17. Put \[ \begin{split} L^\dagger&=\widehat{\pi_1(Y^\dagger,s_0)},\qquad L=\widehat{\pi_1(Y,s_0)},\\ q:L^\dagger&\twoheadrightarrow L,\qquad \Phi^\dagger=\widehat{\phi^\dagger}_*,\\ K^+&=\Phi^\dagger(\ker q) =\Phi^\dagger(L^\dagger)\cap\mathcal J . \end{split} \tag{F.18.6} \] For $u\in\mathcal E$ and any $w\in q^{-1}(u)$, define the actual element \[ b(w)=\ell(u)^{-1}\Phi^\dagger(w)\in\mathcal J . \tag{F.18.7} \] It is the unique solution of \[ b(w)^{-1}R^\dagger(b(w)) =\Phi^\dagger(w)^{-1}R^\dagger(\Phi^\dagger(w)). \tag{F.18.8} \] The right $K^+$-orbit $b(w)K^+$ is independent of $w$ and defines a continuous map \[ \mathfrak o:\mathcal E\longrightarrow\mathcal J/K^+ . \tag{F.18.9} \] No group structure on this coset space is assumed. Its distinguished fibre is exactly \[ \begin{split} \mathfrak o^{-1}(K^+) &=\{u\in\mathcal E: \ell(u)\in\Phi^\dagger(L^\dagger)\}\\ &=q\bigl((\Phi^\dagger)^{-1}(C^\dagger)\bigr). \end{split} \tag{F.18.10} \] These are equalities for the specified full maps. Whether this fibre is all of $\mathcal E$, and whether $\mathcal E$ is trivial, remain unresolved.

statement: An exact cross-divisor action and its finite wreath images — Retain the labelled source, the two-track group, and the subgroups $K^+\leq D^+$ of F.17--F.19. Select the cross divisor between the old point $v_1$ and the positive new point $a$. Its full relative path coordinate is $\mathcal F=\widehat F(x,y,z)$, with the three specified meridians corresponding, in order, to $0,v_\zeta,1$. The actual source $L=\widehat{\pi_1(Y)}=\widehat F_{11}$ has the continuous action \[ A_g(v)=q_g^{-1}\alpha_g(v)p_g \qquad(g\in L,\ v\in\mathcal F), \tag{F.20.1} \] where $\alpha_g,p_g,q_g$ are the literal based braid data specified below. The diagonal-coset map proving this formula, its inverse, and every based source transport are retained in the proof. Let $\mathscr Q$ be the following explicitly enumerated finite quotients of this same $\mathcal F$: the $82$ source-invariant $A_5$ quotients in the enumeration below, all $3,321$ products of two distinct such quotients, and the six mod-two homology-cover quotients \[ Q_\rho=\mathcal F/ \overline{[N_\rho,N_\rho]\,N_\rho^2}, \qquad N_\rho=\ker(\rho:\mathcal F\to A_5), \qquad |Q_\rho|=60\cdot2^{121}, \tag{F.20.2} \] whose four peripheral images under $\rho$ are all nonidentity. Every action (F.20.1) on every member of $\mathscr Q$ is transitive. In each of the six last cases the image of the source filling kernel acts by right translations through a subgroup of index four; the remaining actual source generators connect all four cosets. For each $Q\in\mathscr Q$ and each prime $\ell$ there is an explicitly specified continuous homomorphism \[ \chi_{Q,\ell}:D^+\longrightarrow\mathbb F_\ell[Q] \quad\hbox{with}\quad \chi_{Q,\ell}(K^+)=\chi_{Q,\ell}(D^+)=\mathbb F_\ell[Q]. \tag{F.20.3} \] It is obtained from the actual one-point forgetting map and the finite wreath assignment in (F.20.15) below. The selected meridian has the following actual centralizer-image containment: \[ \varpi\bigl(C_G(\nu_{u,\epsilon})\bigr) \supseteq\mathcal P_{u,\epsilon}. \tag{F.21.3} \] Write $D^+_{\mathrm{nil}}$ for the inverse limit of all continuous finite nilpotent quotients of $D^+$. statement: The actual two-point kernel, its compact generators, and the remaining source map — Retain the original F.19 base configuration. Let $p=a(s_0)$, $n=-a(s_0)$, and let $S'$ be the plane with its seven old finite labels removed. Filling the four labels $U=\{v_u:u\ne\zeta\}$ gives the plane $S$ with the three old finite labels $0,1,v_\zeta$ removed. The actual two-point groups are \[ J=\widehat{\pi_1(\operatorname{Conf}_2(S'),(p,n))},\qquad J_4=\widehat{\pi_1(\operatorname{Conf}_2(S),(p,n))},\qquad D^+=\ker(J\to J_4). \tag{F.22.1} \] There are compatible based point-pushing sections of the two positive-point projections, described below, and geometric free coordinates in which \[ \begin{gathered} V_+=\widehat F(g_1,g_2,g_3,u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4),\qquad Q_+=\widehat F(g_1,g_2,g_3),\\ V=\widehat F(X_1,X_2,X_3,U_1,U_2,U_3,U_4,t),\qquad P=\widehat F(X_1,X_2,X_3,t),\\ R_+=\ker(V_+\to Q_+),\qquad R_1=\ker(V\to P). \end{gathered} \tag{F.22.2} \] The displayed fillings kill precisely $u_j$ and $U_j$, respectively. With the actual section $\sigma:V_+\to J$ and fiber inclusion $\iota:V\to J$, there are mutually inverse continuous maps \[ \begin{aligned} R_1\rtimes R_+&\xrightarrow{\ \Theta\ }D^+, &(b,g)&\longmapsto\iota(b)\sigma(g),\\ D^+&\longrightarrow R_1\rtimes R_+, &d&\longmapsto \bigl(\iota^{-1}(d\sigma(p_+d)^{-1}),p_+d\bigr). \end{aligned} \tag{F.22.3} \] Here $p_+$ forgets the negative point; the action in this semidirect product is the actual conjugation by $\sigma$. Its complete free-word recipe is (F.22.11)--(F.22.12). For a profinite space $T$, write $\mathfrak F(T)$ for the free profinite group on continuous maps from $T$, as constructed in the proof. This definition retains the topology on the generator space. Put $I=\{1,2,3,4\}$. Then the exact compact-generator identifications are \[ \begin{aligned} \mathfrak F(Q_+\times I)&\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R_+, &(q,j)&\longmapsto s_+(q)u_js_+(q)^{-1},\\ \mathfrak F(P\times I)&\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R_1, &(v,j)&\longmapsto s_1(v)U_js_1(v)^{-1}, \end{aligned} \tag{F.22.4} \] where $s_+$ and $s_1$ retain the displayed free generators. The other one-point forgetting is the actual $p_-:J\to V_-$, with \[ \begin{gathered} V_-=\widehat F(X_1,X_2,X_3,U_1,U_2,U_3,U_4),\qquad Q_-=\widehat F(X_1,X_2,X_3),\\ R_-=\ker(V_-\to Q_-),\qquad W=D^+\cap\ker p_+\cap\ker p_- . \end{gathered} \tag{F.22.5} \] One has the exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow W\longrightarrow D^+ \xrightarrow{(p_+,p_-)}R_+\times R_-\longrightarrow1. \tag{F.22.6} \] Inside the actual fiber $V$, let $s_-$ retain $Q_-$ and put $\eta(q,e)=s_-(q)e s_-(q)^{-1}$ for $e\in\{U_1,U_2,U_3,U_4,t\}$. Then \[ W= \overline{\langle\!\langle [\eta(q,U_j),\eta(q',t)] :q,q'\in Q_-,\ j\in I \rangle\!\rangle}_{V} . \tag{F.22.7} \] The literal element $[U_1,t]$ belongs to $W$ and generates a full closed copy of $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$. Finally let $\Delta$ be the sixteen actual source collisions, with the F.19 source meridians and section $j:L\to H^\dagger$. There is a specified continuous map \[ \Lambda:\mathfrak F(L\times\Delta)\longrightarrow D^+, \qquad(l,d)\longmapsto j(l)\nu_dj(l)^{-1}, \qquad\operatorname{im}\Lambda=K^+ . \tag{F.22.8} \] Its coordinates in (F.22.3) are given by the actual two projection formulas there, applied to the displayed element. Thus the remaining equality $K^+=D^+$ is exactly surjectivity of this named continuous homomorphism onto the displayed semidirect product. This statement does not settle that surjectivity or the original residual source-membership equation. Write $\Delta_+$ and $\Delta_-$ for the eight collisions with the positive and negative new point, respectively, and put $\mathcal K_\pm=p_\pm(K^+)$. The exact joint source image is their full direct product: \[ 1\longrightarrow K^+\cap W\longrightarrow K^+ \xrightarrow{(p_+,p_-)}\mathcal K_+\times\mathcal K_- \longrightarrow1 . \tag{F.22.8a} \] Each marginal is the actual image of the corresponding eight-collision source filling kernel, as specified in (F.22.21). Their equality with $R_+$ and $R_-$ remains unresolved.

statement: All-field rank-one cocycles and the actual marginal affine fixed points — Retain the actual continuous inclusions $\mathcal K_\pm\leq R_\pm\leq V_\pm$ and the source maps of F.19--F.23. Let $k$ be a finite field, with its discrete topology, and let $\chi:V_\pm\to k^\times$ be a continuous character whose restriction to $R_\pm$ is nontrivial. Give the additive group of $k$ the left action $g\cdot b=\chi(g)b$, and denote this module by $k_\chi$. The actual restriction maps are injective: \[ \begin{aligned} Z^1_{\mathrm{cont}}(V_\pm,k_\chi)&\longrightarrow Z^1_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathcal K_\pm,k_{\chi|\mathcal K_\pm}),\\ H^1_{\mathrm{cont}}(V_\pm,k_\chi)&\longrightarrow H^1_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathcal K_\pm,k_{\chi|\mathcal K_\pm}). \end{aligned} \tag{F.24.1} \] Here a crossed homomorphism satisfies $d(gh)=d(g)+\chi(g)d(h)$, and the principal crossed homomorphisms are $d_b(g)=(\chi(g)-1)b$, for $b\in k$. Write $\operatorname{Aff}_1(k)=k\rtimes k^\times$, acting on $k$ by $(b,a)z=b+az$, and let $T_k=\{(b,1):b\in k\}$ be its translation subgroup. For every continuous homomorphism $\rho:V_\pm\to\operatorname{Aff}_1(k)$ one has \[ \operatorname{Fix}_k\rho(\mathcal K_\pm) =\operatorname{Fix}_k\rho(R_\pm). \tag{F.24.2} \] For the representations whose scalar character is nontrivial on $R_\pm$, both sides also equal $\operatorname{Fix}_k\rho(V_\pm)$. For every representation in the specified class \[ \left\{\rho\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}} (V_\pm,\operatorname{Aff}_1(k)): \rho(\mathcal K_\pm)\cap T_k=\{1\}\right\}, \] the exact marginal images agree: \[ \rho(\mathcal K_\pm)=\rho(R_\pm). \tag{F.24.3} \] The coefficient calculation proving (F.24.1) has integer Laurent coefficients and proves its rank assertion over every field, including characteristics two and three. Its input is the literal negative marginal braid data of F.23, with the same source lassos and comparison maps. The positive assertion is transported by the explicit F.23.13 isomorphism. The full marginal equalities and the equality $K^+=D^+$ remain unresolved.

statement: The actual affine marginal images with a common scalar field — Retain $\mathcal K_\pm\leq R_\pm\leq V_\pm$ and their actual maps from F.19--F.24. statement: The exact trace obstruction and all affine marginal images with scalar field of order nine — Retain the actual inclusions $\mathcal K_\pm\leq R_\pm\leq V_\pm$ of F.19--F.25. Fix either sign, and temporarily write these groups as $K\leq R\leq V$. A proper affine marginal image $\rho(K)\subsetneq\rho(R)$, for a continuous $\rho:V\to\operatorname{Aff}_1(k)$ over a finite field, has an actual continuous affine image of the following form: \[ \begin{gathered} \rho':V\longrightarrow k_0\rtimes D,\qquad \rho'(V)=k_0\rtimes D,\qquad \rho'(R)=k_0\rtimes C,\\ \rho'(K)\ \leq\ \ker\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/k_1}:k_0\to k_1\bigr) \rtimes C,\\ C=\chi(R)=\chi(K)\ne\{1\},\qquad D=\chi(V),\qquad k_1=\mathbb F_p(C)\subsetneq k_0=\mathbb F_p(D). \end{gathered} \tag{F.26.1} \] Here $\chi$ is the original scalar character, retained by the explicit conjugation and coefficient map constructed below. In particular the last group in (F.26.1) is a proper subgroup of the displayed $R$ image. For any finite-field data $k_0,\chi,C,k_1$ as in (F.26.1), including the equality case $k_1=k_0$, put $q_1=|k_1|$ and $m=[k_0:k_1]$. The exact coefficient map is \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr T_\chi: Z^1_{\rm cont}(V,k_{0,\chi})&\longrightarrow Z^1_{\rm cont}(K,k_{1,\chi|K}),\\ d&\longmapsto\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/k_1}(d|K). \end{aligned} \tag{F.26.2} \] Its known kernel subspace is \[ \mathscr P_\chi= \{\,g\mapsto(\chi(g)-1)b: b\in k_0,\ \operatorname{Tr}(b)=0\,\}. \tag{F.26.3} \] Every element of $\ker\mathscr T_\chi\setminus\mathscr P_\chi$ gives a proper actual affine marginal image, and every proper affine marginal image gives such an element for the data in (F.26.1). Thus $\ker\mathscr T_\chi=\mathscr P_\chi$ for all the stated data is an exact remaining criterion for the full scalar affine image equality. The proof gives an explicit coefficient isomorphism identifying this criterion with the summed restrictions for the distinct characters $\chi^{q_1^j}$, $0\leq j<m$. Its rank target is $6m+1$ on $7m$ columns; no general attainment of that rank is asserted here. For the scalar field of order nine that rank is attained. More precisely, for every finite field $k$ and every continuous $\rho:V_\pm\to\operatorname{Aff}_1(k)$ whose scalar values generate a subfield of order nine, \[ \rho(\mathcal K_\pm)=\rho(R_\pm). \tag{F.26.4} \] Consequently this equality holds for every continuous map $V_\pm\to\operatorname{Aff}_1(\mathbb F_9)$, including maps whose scalar field is $\mathbb F_3$. The finite calculation proving the additional field case exhausts exactly $7\,560$ character tuples and retains the literal F.23 source automorphisms.

statement: All finite affine marginal images on an exact two-parameter character locus — Use the actual negative free basis $X_1,\ldots,X_7$ of F.24 and the based comparison $\mathcal B_+:V_-\to V_+$ of F.23.13. The character locus \[ \chi(Y_1^\pm)=\chi(Y_4^\pm)=\chi(Y_5^\pm) =\chi(Y_6^\pm)=1,\qquad \chi(Y_2^\pm)\chi(Y_3^\pm)\chi(Y_7^\pm)=1 \tag{F.27.1} \] has the exact image equality \[ \rho(\mathcal K_\pm)=\rho(R_\pm). \tag{F.27.2} \] There is no restriction on the characteristic, extension degree, or size of the original coefficient field. More precisely, write a negative character in this locus as $(1,s,t,1,1,1,c^{-1})$, where $c=st$, and put $k_0=\mathbb F_p(s,t)$, $k_1=\mathbb F_p(c)$. For $c\ne1$ and $k_1\subsetneq k_0$, let $q_1=|k_1|$, $m=[k_0:k_1]$ and $\chi_j=\chi^{q_1^j}$, $0\leq j<m$. Put $C=\chi(R_\pm)$, $k_1=\mathbb F_p(C)$ and $k_0=\mathbb F_p(\chi(V_\pm))$. For $C\ne\{1\}$, let $q_1=|k_1|$, $m=[k_0:k_1]$ and $\chi_j=\chi^{q_1^j}$, $0\leq j<m$. The summed continuous $H^1$ restriction for these characters is injective. The corresponding cocycle restriction has exactly the principal tuples with parameter sum zero as its kernel, and has rank $6m+1$ on $7m$ coordinates.

statement: Exact paired restriction kernel for opposite first characters — Use the actual bases $Y_i^-=X_i$ and $Y_i^+=\mathcal B_+(X_i)$ of F.23.13. Let $k$ be a finite field of odd characteristic, and let $\chi,\chi':V_\pm\to k^\times$ be the continuous characters with values \[ \begin{aligned} (\chi(Y_i^\pm))_{i=1}^7&=(r,s,t,u,v,w,z),\\ (\chi'(Y_i^\pm))_{i=1}^7&=(-r,s,t,u,v,w,z),\qquad \langle u,v,w,z\rangle\ne\{1\}. \end{aligned} \tag{F.33.1} \] All seven displayed values are nonzero; $r^2=1$ is included. The two characters have the same restriction $\eta$ to the actual subgroup $\mathcal K_\pm$. The summed continuous cocycle restriction has the exact kernel \[ \begin{split} \ker\bigl[Z^1_\chi(V_\pm,k)\oplus Z^1_{\chi'}(V_\pm,k) &\longrightarrow Z^1_\eta(\mathcal K_\pm,k)\bigr]\\ &=\{(b(\chi-1),-b(\chi'-1)):b\in k\}. \end{split} \tag{F.33.2} \] It has dimension one, and the restriction map has rank $13$ on the original $14$ generator coordinates. The induced summed $H^1$ restriction is injective. More generally, the explicit $64$ by $13$ Laurent matrix used below has rank $13$ over every field, in every characteristic, for every nonzero tuple $(R,s,t,u,v,w,z)$ with $(u,v,w,z)\ne(1,1,1,1)$.
